title: Herb-butter roast turkey
description: A whole turkey roasted over onions and citrus, with thyme-sage butter under the skin so the breast stays juicy.
notes: Plan about 15 minutes per 500 g after the first hour. Save the pan juices for gravy.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C. Pat the turkey dry inside and out, then season the cavity with salt.
Mash the butter with chopped thyme, sage, garlic, salt and pepper. Loosen the breast skin and spread most of the butter underneath.
Tuck onion wedges and lemon halves into the cavity. Set the turkey on a rack over the remaining onion.
Roast until the thickest thigh reads 75°C, tenting the breast with foil if it browns too fast.
Rest the turkey 30 minutes before carving so the juices settle back into the meat.

title: Maple-glazed baked ham
description: A smoked ham scored and lacquered with maple, mustard and clove for Christmas or Sunday supper.
notes: Use leftover bone for a pot of beans the next day.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C. Score the ham fat in a diamond pattern and stud a few intersections with cloves.
Stir maple syrup, brown sugar, mustard and vinegar into a thick glaze.
Bake the ham covered for 70 minutes, then uncover and brush with glaze every 15 minutes.
Finish until the crust is glossy and the centre is piping hot.
Rest 15 minutes, then slice across the grain so each piece keeps a ribbon of glaze.

title: Sausage and sage stuffing
description: Toasted bread, browned sausage and lots of sage baked until the edges crisp and the centre stays moist.
notes: Bake separately rather than inside the bird so both cook evenly.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C. Tear the bread into chunks and dry them on a tray for 10 minutes.
Brown the sausage, then soften onion and celery in the butter with chopped sage.
Toss bread with the pan mixture, beaten eggs and enough stock to moisten without soupiness.
Bake in a buttered dish until the top is deep gold and the centre is set.
Rest 10 minutes so slices hold together on the plate.

title: Creamy mashed potatoes
description: Floury potatoes mashed with warm butter and milk until they sit in soft peaks.
notes: 500 g plus 1 kg potatoes in other recipes will merge on the grocery list.
steps: Peel the potatoes, cut into even chunks and start them in cold salted water.
Simmer until a knife slides through, then drain thoroughly and return to the hot pan to steam dry.
Warm the milk with butter. Mash the potatoes and beat in the dairy until smooth.
Season with salt and white pepper. Do not add cold milk or the mash turns gluey.
Cover and keep warm; loosen with a splash more hot milk just before serving.

title: Brown-butter green beans with almonds
description: Blanched beans tossed in nutty brown butter and toasted almonds — a lighter Christmas side.
notes: Skip almonds if anyone at the table has a nut allergy.
steps: Trim the beans and boil in salted water until just tender, then plunge into ice water.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan until they smell sweet, then tip them out.
Melt the butter in the same pan and cook until the milk solids turn hazelnut brown.
Toss in the drained beans, lemon zest and almonds. Finish with lemon juice and salt.
Serve immediately so the butter stays foamy and the beans stay bright.

title: Jellied cranberry sauce
description: Fresh cranberries cooked with orange and sugar until they set into a sliceable sauce.
notes: Make this two days ahead; the flavour rounds out overnight.
steps: Combine cranberries, sugar, orange juice, a strip of orange zest and salt in a saucepan.
Cook over medium heat until the berries burst and the liquid looks syrupy.
Mash lightly, then simmer 3 minutes more so the natural pectin can set.
Pour into a small bowl, cool, then refrigerate until firm enough to unmould.
Slice or spoon beside roast meat. It keeps 5 days chilled.

title: Sweet potato bake with pecan crumb
description: Mashed sweet potato under a pecan-oat crumb — festive without marshmallow.
notes: Use gluten-free oats if needed.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Roast or boil the sweet potatoes until completely soft, then mash with half the butter, maple, cinnamon and salt.
Spread the mash in a baking dish.
Chop pecans and rub them with oats and the remaining butter into a rough crumb.
Scatter the crumb on top and bake until the nuts smell toasted and the edges bubble.
Rest 10 minutes so scoops stay neat.

title: Classic pumpkin pie
description: Spiced pumpkin custard in a short crust — the Thanksgiving close that also belongs on a winter table.
notes: Use plain pumpkin puree, not pumpkin pie filling.
steps: Rub butter into flour and salt, add a spoon of ice water, and rest the dough 30 minutes.
Line a pie tin, prick the base, and chill while you beat pumpkin, milk, sugar, eggs and spice.
Blind-bake the crust 12 minutes at 190°C, then lower the oven to 170°C.
Pour in the filling and bake until the centre barely wobbles.
Cool completely so the custard slices cleanly. Serve at cool room temperature.

title: Pecan pie
description: A buttery crust holding a dark sugar filling and a tight layer of pecans.
notes: A pinch of salt in the filling keeps the pie from tasting flat.
steps: Make a short crust, line a tin, and chill it while the oven heats to 180°C.
Whisk eggs, brown sugar, syrup, melted butter, vanilla and salt until smooth.
Scatter pecans in the shell and pour the filling over so nuts rise to the top.
Bake until the centre is just set and the nuts look lacquered.
Cool to room temperature before slicing; the filling finishes setting as it cools.

title: Spiced apple cider
description: Fresh cider simmered with orange, cinnamon and clove — alcohol-free and house-filling.
notes: Use fresh cider, not apple juice from concentrate, if you can.
steps: Pour the cider into a pot with orange slices, cinnamon, cloves, star anise and sugar.
Bring to a bare simmer — do not boil or the cider turns harsh.
Steep 20 minutes, then taste and add a little more sugar only if the apples were very tart.
Strain into mugs or a thermos.
Keep extra on the lowest heat with the spices parked in a tea ball.

title: Sage and citrus roast turkey
description: A British Christmas bird rubbed with sage butter and roasted over citrus and onion for a moist, fragrant table centre.
notes: Weigh the turkey and allow about 15 minutes per 500 g after the first hour.
steps: Pat the turkey dry, season the cavity with salt, and stuff it with onion wedges, orange halves and thyme sprigs.
Mash the butter with chopped sage, pepper and remaining salt, then spread it under the breast skin and over the legs.
Roast at 180°C on a rack until the thickest thigh reaches 75°C, tenting the breast if the sage butter browns too fast.
Rest the bird at least 30 minutes so juices settle, then carve and spoon the citrus pan juices over the slices.
Skim the roasting tin for gravy rather than washing away the orange and sage fond.

title: Pigs in blankets
description: Chipolatas wrapped in streaky bacon and roasted until the pork fat crackles — the side that vanishes first.
notes: Assemble the night before and keep covered in the fridge.
steps: Stretch each rasher of streaky bacon and wrap it once around a chipolata, overlapping the seam.
Set the parcels seam-side down in a tin and grind black pepper over the bacon.
Roast at 200°C until the bacon is bronzed and the sausages are cooked through, about 25 minutes.
Brush with honey for the last five minutes if you want a sticky sheen, then drain briefly on paper.
Serve around the turkey while the bacon still crackles.

title: Goose-fat roast potatoes
description: Floury potatoes parboiled, roughened and roasted in goose fat until the edges shatter and the centres stay fluffy.
notes: Duck fat works if goose fat is scarce; olive oil is a lighter stand-in.
steps: Peel the potatoes, cut into large even chunks, and start them in cold salted water.
Parboil until the edges soften, drain well, then shake the colander so the surfaces fluff.
Heat goose fat in a roasting tin until shimmering, tumble in the potatoes, rosemary and pepper.
Roast at 200°C, turning once, until deep gold and audibly crisp, then toss with flaky salt.
Do not crowd the tin or the potatoes steam instead of roasting.

title: Brussels sprouts with bacon and chestnuts
description: Halved sprouts sautéed with smoked bacon and sweet chestnuts so the brassicas pick up caramelised edges.
notes: Skip bacon and use extra butter plus salt for a vegetarian pan.
steps: Trim the sprouts, halve them, and blanch for two minutes in salted water, then drain thoroughly.
Render the bacon in a wide pan until the fat runs, then add butter and the sprouts cut-side down.
When the cut faces brown, fold in crumbled chestnuts and black pepper.
Cook until the chestnuts are hot and glossy and the sprouts are tender but still green.
Serve at once so the bacon stays crisp rather than steaming.

title: Yorkshire puddings
description: A well-rested batter poured into smoking-hot fat so the puddings billow high with crisp walls and custardy centres.
notes: Resting the batter is what gives the rise, not extra flour.
steps: Whisk flour, eggs, milk and salt into a smooth batter and rest it at least 30 minutes.
Heat a spoon of beef dripping in each hole of a muffin tin in a 220°C oven until the fat smokes.
Pour batter in quickly so it hits the hot fat and starts to puff at the edges.
Bake without opening the door until the puddings are tall, deep gold and set in the middle.
Serve immediately; they collapse if they wait under a lid.

title: Mince pies
description: Buttery shortcrust cases filled with spiced mincemeat and baked until the pastry smells of butter and citrus peel.
notes: Mincemeat pies freeze unbaked; bake from frozen and add a few minutes.
steps: Rub cold butter into flour and salt until sandy, bind with a spoon of ice water, and chill the dough 30 minutes.
Roll thinly, cut lids and bases, and line a bun tin without stretching the pastry.
Spoon mincemeat into each case, cover with a lid, and crimp; brush with beaten egg and a dust of sugar.
Bake at 190°C until the pastry is biscuit-gold and the filling bubbles at the seams.
Cool a few minutes in the tin so the cases set before you lift them.

title: Steamed Christmas pudding
description: A dark steamed pudding packed with vine fruit, suet and spice, meant to be made ahead and flamed at the table.
notes: Make at least a week ahead; the flavour deepens as it sits.
steps: Toss raisins, currants, suet, sugar, breadcrumbs, flour and mixed spice in a large bowl.
Beat in the eggs and brandy until the mixture looks glossy and holds when pressed.
Pack into a buttered pudding basin, cover with pleated parchment and foil, and tie tightly.
Steam for six hours, topping up the water so the pan never boils dry, then cool and store wrapped.
Re-steam for two hours on Christmas Day and turn out onto a warm plate to flame.

title: Spiced mulled wine
description: Red wine warmed with orange, cinnamon and clove — fragrant, not boiled, for a Christmas-eve jug.
notes: A cheap fruity red works better than a tannic bottle.
steps: Pour the wine into a pan with orange slices, cinnamon, cloves, star anise and sugar.
Warm to a bare shiver — never a rolling boil — so the alcohol and perfume stay in the jug.
Steep 15 minutes, taste, and add a little more sugar only if the wine is very tart.
Strain into heatproof glasses, returning one cinnamon stick to the jug for serving.
Keep leftover wine on the lowest heat with spices parked in a tea ball.

title: Smoked salmon with capers and rye
description: Cold-smoked salmon arranged with capers, lemon and buttered rye — a quiet Christmas starter that needs no pan.
notes: Buy the salmon the day you serve it and keep it well wrapped.
steps: Butter the rye bread lightly and cut it into neat fingers or small squares.
Fold the smoked salmon into loose ribbons rather than stacking flat slices.
Scatter capers and torn dill over the salmon and finish with lemon zest and a squeeze of juice.
Serve immediately with black pepper at the table so the lemon stays bright.
Keep the salmon chilled until the last minute; warmth dulls the smoke.

title: Clove-studded bread sauce
description: Milk infused with onion and clove, then thickened with breadcrumbs into the pale sauce that belongs beside roast turkey.
notes: Make the infusion in the morning and finish the crumbs just before carving.
steps: Stud the onion with cloves and simmer it gently in the milk for 15 minutes so the dairy takes on perfume.
Lift out the onion, then stir in breadcrumbs, butter, nutmeg and salt.
Cook on low until the sauce is thick enough to mound on a spoon but still pourable.
Rest five minutes; it thickens further as the crumbs swell.
Loosen with a splash of hot milk if it sits, and keep it covered so a skin does not form.

title: Honey-roast parsnips
description: Parsnip batons roasted until sweet, then lacquered with honey so the edges caramelise without burning.
notes: Crowding makes them steam; use two tins if needed.
steps: Peel the parsnips, quarter them lengthways, and cut out any woody cores.
Toss with olive oil, salt and thyme, then roast at 200°C until the tips brown.
Drizzle honey over the tin, toss once, and return to the oven for eight minutes.
Watch closely so the honey darkens to amber rather than black.
Serve from the tin while the glaze is still sticky.

title: Glazed Christmas carrots
description: Whole or batoned carrots simmered then finished in butter and a little sugar until they shine.
notes: A pinch of cumin is optional if you want a warmer spice note.
steps: Peel the carrots and cut them into even batons so they cook at the same pace.
Simmer in salted water until just tender, then drain well.
Melt butter with sugar in a wide pan, add the carrots, and toss until each piece is coated.
Cook a few minutes more until the glaze clings and the edges look lacquered.
Finish with chopped parsley and serve hot beside the roast.

title: Cauliflower cheese
description: Blanched cauliflower baked under a sharp cheddar sauce until the top blisters and the florets stay intact.
notes: Mustard powder sharpens the cheese without making a mustard sauce.
steps: Break the cauliflower into florets and blanch until a knife meets slight resistance, then drain hard.
Make a roux with butter and flour, whisk in milk, and simmer until the sauce coats a spoon.
Stir in most of the cheddar, mustard powder and salt, then fold the sauce over the florets in a dish.
Scatter remaining cheddar and bake at 190°C until the top is blistered and bubbling.
Rest five minutes so scoops hold rather than flooding the plate.

title: Sage and onion stuffing balls
description: Breadcrumb stuffing with fried onion and plenty of sage, rolled into balls that crisp in the oven beside the bird.
notes: Bake separately from the turkey so both cook evenly.
steps: Soften the onion in butter until sweet, then cool slightly.
Mix breadcrumbs with chopped sage, salt, pepper, the onion and beaten egg until the mix holds.
Roll into walnut-sized balls and space them on a greased tray.
Bake at 190°C until the outsides are crisp and the centres stay moist.
Turn once if the undersides pale; they should be gold all over.

title: Turkey giblet gravy
description: A deep gravy started from giblets and finished with roasting-tin juices so it tastes of the bird, not stock cubes.
notes: Start the giblet stock while the turkey goes in.
steps: Simmer giblets (not the liver) with onion, carrot, thyme and water for an hour, then strain.
When the turkey rests, pour tin juices into a jug and skim most of the fat, keeping two spoons.
Cook flour in that fat until it smells toasted, then whisk in the giblet stock and juices.
Simmer until the gravy is glossy and coats a spoon; season with salt.
Strain if you want it silk-smooth, or leave the browned bits for flavour.

title: Brandy butter
description: Soft butter beaten with icing sugar and brandy until pale — the cold sauce for hot Christmas pudding.
notes: Keeps a week chilled; bring it out 20 minutes before pudding.
steps: Beat the butter until it is almost white and very soft.
Sift in icing sugar in two additions, beating until the mixture is fluffy.
Beat in brandy a little at a time so the emulsion does not split, then add nutmeg.
Chill until firm enough to spoon, but not rock-hard.
Serve a cold knob on each slice of hot pudding so it melts into a sauce.

title: Sherry trifle
description: Sponge soaked in sherry, layered with fruit, thick custard and cream — a make-ahead bowl for Boxing Day as well as Christmas.
notes: Build it the night before; add almonds at the last minute.
steps: Lay sponge in a glass bowl, spoon over sherry, and scatter raspberries so they settle into the cake.
Warm milk, whisk yolks with sugar, then cook the custard until it thickly coats a spoon; cool slightly.
Pour custard over the fruit and chill until the layer is set enough to take cream.
Whip double cream to soft peaks and spoon it on generously.
Toast flaked almonds and scatter them just before serving so they stay crisp.

title: Iced Christmas cake
description: A dense fruit cake matured with brandy, then covered in marzipan and a simple white icing for the centre of the table.
notes: Bake in November if you can; the cake improves as it sits.
steps: Soak the dried fruit in brandy overnight so every piece is plump.
Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs, then fold in flour, spice and the soaked fruit.
Bake in a lined tin at 140°C until a skewer comes out clean, about three hours; cool in the tin.
Feed with a spoon of brandy, wrap, and mature at least a week.
Cover with rolled marzipan, then a thick icing made from icing sugar and a little water; let it set overnight.

title: Hot rum sauce for pudding
description: A pourable butter sauce spiked with rum for people who want Christmas pudding without hard brandy butter.
notes: Use a rum you would drink; cooking rum tastes thin.
steps: Melt butter with brown sugar until the sugar dissolves and the mix looks like dark caramel.
Pour in cream and simmer one minute until the sauce is smooth.
Take off the heat and stir in rum and salt.
Keep warm in a jug; it thickens as it cools, so loosen with a drop of cream if needed.
Pour over slices of pudding at the table rather than drowning the plate in the kitchen.

title: Roast goose with apples
description: A dry-skinned goose roasted until the fat renders, with apples in the cavity to perfume the meat.
notes: A goose yields less meat than a turkey of the same weight; plan sides generously.
steps: Prick the goose skin all over without piercing the meat, and season generously with salt and pepper.
Stuff the cavity with apple wedges, onion and sage, then set the bird on a rack over a deep tin.
Roast at 180°C, pouring off fat twice, until the skin is mahogany and the thighs read 75°C.
Rest 30 minutes; the apples will have collapsed into a sharp spooning sauce.
Save the poured-off fat for roast potatoes the next day.

title: Clove-crusted roast gammon
description: Gammon simmered then roasted with a mustard-sugar crust studded with cloves — the Boxing Day cold cut as well as the hot roast.
notes: Taste the simmering water after 30 minutes; if it is fiercely salty, change it once.
steps: Cover the gammon with water, add onion and bay, and simmer gently until tender, about two hours.
Lift, cool slightly, then peel off the rind leaving a layer of fat; score diamonds and stud with cloves.
Mix brown sugar and mustard, spread over the fat, and roast at 200°C until the crust is lacquered.
Rest 20 minutes before carving hot, or cool completely for cold slices.
Strain a mug of the simmering liquor; it seasons cabbage or beans later.

title: Prawn cocktail
description: Chilled prawns on shredded lettuce with a sharp tomato-mayonnaise sauce — a retro starter that still earns its place.
notes: Pat prawns dry so the sauce does not slide off.
steps: Stir mayonnaise, ketchup, Worcestershire and a squeeze of lemon into a pale pink sauce.
Shred the lettuce and divide it between chilled glasses or small bowls.
Fold most of the prawns through a little sauce, then pile them on the lettuce.
Spoon remaining sauce over the top and finish with lemon zest.
Keep everything cold; the dish is about contrast, not warmth.

title: Potted shrimp
description: Brown shrimp set in spiced butter so they keep for a make-ahead Christmas-eve nibble with toast.
notes: Clarify the butter if you want a longer fridge life.
steps: Melt the butter gently with mace and cayenne until it smells warm, not fried.
Stir in the shrimp just to heat them through, then spoon into small pots.
Pour remaining butter over so the shrimp sit under a seal; chill until firm.
Turn out or serve in the pot with hot toast and lemon wedges.
The butter seal keeps them two days in the fridge.

title: Smoked mackerel pâté
description: Smoked mackerel beaten with cream cheese and lemon into a spreadable pâté for crackers or rye.
notes: A teaspoon of horseradish wakes it up if the fish is very mild.
steps: Skin the mackerel and flake it, checking for bones.
Beat cream cheese with lemon zest and juice until loosened.
Fold in the fish, chopped dill and pepper; leave some flakes visible.
Chill 20 minutes so it firms enough to scoop.
Serve with rye or cucumber rounds, not only crackers.

title: Spiced braised red cabbage
description: Red cabbage braised slowly with apple, vinegar and spice until it is jammy enough to sit beside goose or turkey.
notes: This is one of the best make-ahead Christmas sides.
steps: Shred the cabbage finely and peel and slice the apples.
Layer cabbage, apple, sugar, salt and cinnamon in a heavy pan, then pour over vinegar.
Cover and cook on low for an hour, stirring once, until the cabbage is silky.
Uncover for ten minutes if the pan is watery; you want a glossy braid, not soup.
Reheat gently on the day; the flavour is better after a night in the fridge.

title: Chestnut and sage stuffing
description: A British stuffing of sausage meat, chestnuts and sage baked in a dish so the top crisps.
notes: Use good sausage meat; cheap mixes turn greasy.
steps: Soften the onion, then mix with sausage meat, chopped chestnuts, breadcrumbs, sage and egg.
Press into a buttered dish without packing it like concrete.
Bake at 180°C until the top is brown and the centre is cooked through.
Rest ten minutes, then spoon or cut into squares.
The chestnuts should stay in chunks, not vanish into paste.

title: Citrus-brined turkey crown
description: A turkey crown soaked in a light citrus brine, then roasted so smaller households still get proper white meat.
notes: Skip brining if the crown was pre-salted by the butcher.
steps: Dissolve salt and sugar in water with orange and lemon slices, then brine the crown 8 hours chilled.
Rinse, dry thoroughly, and rub with butter and pepper.
Roast at 180°C until the thickest part of the breast is 74°C.
Rest 25 minutes tented loosely with foil.
Carve in long slices across the grain so the brine-juicy meat does not shred.

title: Cranberry-studded nut roast
description: A compact loaf of mixed nuts, lentils and cranberries that slices cleanly as a vegetarian Christmas main.
notes: Toast the nuts first if they taste flat.
steps: Chop the nuts coarsely and soften the onion until sweet.
Mix nuts, lentils, cranberries, breadcrumbs, thyme, onion and eggs; season well.
Pack into a lined loaf tin and bake at 180°C until the top is firm and browned.
Rest 15 minutes before turning out so slices hold.
Serve with vegetarian gravy and the same roast potatoes as the rest of the table.

title: Mushroom puff wellington
description: A vegan-friendly mushroom and walnut filling wrapped in puff pastry as a centrepiece instead of a bird.
notes: Cool filling is what stops a soggy bottom.
steps: Cook mushrooms and onion in oil until all their liquid evaporates and they smell meaty.
Chop walnuts and thyme into the pan, season, and cool the filling completely.
Roll puff pastry, pile the filling in a log, and seal the seam underneath.
Bake at 200°C until the pastry is deep gold and the base sounds hollow.
Rest ten minutes before slicing with a serrated knife.

title: Sticky toffee pudding
description: Date sponge baked and drowned in a dark toffee sauce — a winter pudding that is not Christmas pudding.
notes: Reheats gently; add a splash of cream to the leftover sauce.
steps: Soak chopped dates in hot water with bicarbonate, then mash them to a loose paste.
Cream butter and half the sugar, beat in eggs, then fold in flour and the date paste.
Bake at 180°C until the sponge springs back.
Simmer remaining sugar with cream into a dark sauce and pour half over the hot sponge.
Serve extra sauce in a jug; the pudding should sit in a shallow pool, not a swamp.

title: Brandy snap baskets
description: Lace-thin ginger biscuits shaped over cups while hot, then filled with cream for a light Christmas pudding alternative.
notes: Work quickly; once cold they will not bend.
steps: Melt butter, syrup and sugar, then stir in flour and ginger to a smooth batter.
Spoon small rounds onto a lined tray, leaving wide gaps; they spread into lace.
Bake at 180°C until deep gold, then lift each biscuit over an upturned cup to set as a basket.
Cool completely so they crisp.
Whip cream and fill the baskets just before serving or they soften.

title: Shortbread fingers
description: A three-ingredient Scottish biscuit baked pale and sandy, then cut into fingers while warm.
notes: Overbaking turns them bitter; pale is correct.
steps: Beat butter and sugar until just combined, then work in flour and salt without whipping air.
Press into a shallow tin and prick all over with a fork.
Bake at 160°C until the shortbread is set and only faintly gold.
Cut into fingers while warm, then cool in the tin so the edges stay sharp.
Dust with a little extra sugar while still warm if you like a crust.

title: Gingerbread people
description: Cut-out gingerbread figures with a snappy spice dough that children can decorate after tea.
notes: Chill cut-outs on the tray if your kitchen is warm.
steps: Melt butter with sugar and syrup, then mix into flour, ginger, bicarbonate and egg to a firm dough.
Chill 30 minutes, roll to 5 mm, and cut people; lift them onto a lined tray.
Bake at 180°C until the edges darken slightly and the centres look dry.
Cool on the tray so they firm up before you move them.
Decorate when completely cold so icing does not slide.

title: Mulled cider with orange
description: Dry cider warmed with orange, ginger and cinnamon for a lighter jug than mulled wine.
notes: Choose a dry cider; sweet supermarket cider becomes cloying when warmed.
steps: Pour cider into a pan with orange slices, sliced ginger, cinnamon, cloves and sugar.
Warm slowly until steaming; do not boil or the cider turns harsh.
Steep 15 minutes and taste for sweetness.
Strain into mugs, leaving one cinnamon stick in the jug.
Keep on the lowest heat for late arrivals.

title: Boxing Day turkey pie
description: Leftover turkey and ham in a mustardy sauce under puff pastry — the pie that justifies cooking a large bird.
notes: A handful of leftover stuffing under the lid is a good addition.
steps: Make a sauce with butter, flour and stock, then stir in mustard.
Fold in chopped turkey and ham; the filling should be thick, not soupy.
Cool slightly, then spoon into a pie dish and cover with puff pastry, sealing the rim.
Bake at 200°C until the pastry is risen and deep gold.
Rest ten minutes so the sauce settles when you cut.

title: Bubble and squeak
description: Boxing Day breakfast cakes of leftover potato and greens fried until the crust is almost burnt in the best way.
notes: Wet leftovers will not brown; dry them in a pan first if needed.
steps: Chop roast potatoes and cabbage together so some potato mashes and some stays chunky.
Season with salt and pepper.
Heat butter in a pan and press the mix into a thick cake or smaller rounds.
Fry without poking until a dark crust forms, then flip once.
Serve with a fried egg if you want, or cold ham from the gammon.

title: Boxing Day turkey broth
description: The carcass simmered with leek and barley into a clear, restoring soup the day after the feast.
notes: Cool and lift fat from the top if you want a lighter bowl.
steps: Cover the carcass with water, add leek tops and one carrot, and simmer 70 minutes; strain.
Return the broth to the pan with barley and diced remaining carrot and leek.
Cook until the barley is tender and the vegetables are soft.
Season with salt and finish with parsley.
Pick any remaining meat from the bones into the bowls.

title: Christmas sausage rolls
description: Sausage meat with sage rolled in puff pastry, sliced into party lengths for the drinks table.
notes: Freeze unbaked rolls on a tray, then bag them for emergency guests.
steps: Mix sausage meat with chopped sage and pepper.
Roll pastry into a rectangle, lay a sausage-meat log along one side, and roll to seal.
Brush with beaten egg, cut into lengths, and slash the tops.
Bake at 200°C until the pastry is gold and the meat is cooked through.
Cool slightly so the pastry sets before you pile them on a plate.

title: Thyme cheese straws
description: Cheddar pastry twisted into straws that bake into a salty nibble beside mulled wine.
notes: Grate the cheese finely so the pastry stays even.
steps: Rub butter into flour, then mix in grated cheddar, thyme and cayenne.
Bring together with a spoon of cold water and chill 20 minutes.
Roll, cut into strips, and twist each strip twice.
Bake at 190°C until the straws are deep gold and smell toasty.
Cool on a rack so they crisp; they soften in a sealed tin while warm.

title: Fresh cranberry-orange relish
description: Raw cranberries chopped with orange and sugar into a sharp relish that cuts through roast meat better than jelly.
notes: Do not cook this one; heat dulls the berry snap.
steps: Pulse cranberries until they are coarsely chopped, not puréed.
Zest the orange over the bowl, then peel and chop the flesh, discarding pith.
Stir in sugar and salt and leave an hour so juices run.
Taste; it should be sharp-sweet, not a jam.
Keeps three days chilled; stir before serving.

title: Horseradish cream
description: Cold cream folded with grated horseradish for roast beef or smoked fish on Christmas Eve.
notes: Jarred horseradish works if you drain it well.
steps: Whip the cream to soft peaks; stop before it turns grainy.
Grate horseradish finely and fold it through with vinegar and salt.
Taste after five minutes; horseradish blooms as it sits.
Chill until serving so it stays spoonable.
Serve in a small bowl, not on the meat in the kitchen, so people can take what they want.

title: Roast rib of beef
description: A standing rib roasted hot then slower, rested until the juices stay in the slice — an alternative to turkey.
notes: Ask the butcher to French the bones if you want a neater joint.
steps: Bring the rib to room temperature, rub with oil, salt, pepper and rosemary, and sit it on onion slices.
Roast 20 minutes at 220°C, then lower to 160°C until the centre is 52°C for pink.
Rest at least 30 minutes, loosely tented, before carving between the bones.
Spoon the oniony juices over the slices.
Use a thermometer; time alone lies with thick ribs.

title: Clootie dumpling
description: A Scottish suet dumpling tied in cloth, simmered until dense with spice and dried fruit, then dried by the fire or in a low oven.
notes: The cloth must be wrung in boiling water and floured or the dumpling sticks.
steps: Mix flour, suet, fruit, sugar and spice, then bind with egg and enough milk to make a stiff dough.
Turn onto a scalded, floured cloth, gather into a round, and tie with room to swell.
Simmer in a large pan of water for three hours, topping up as needed.
Unwrap carefully and dry the skin in a low oven until it is no longer wet.
Slice thickly and serve with cream or custard.

title: Welsh rarebit supper
description: A mustardy cheese sauce grilled on toast until it blisters — a late Christmas-eve supper or Boxing Day lunch.
notes: Stale bread holds the topping better than very fresh slices.
steps: Melt butter, stir in flour, then whisk in ale to a thick sauce.
Add cheddar and mustard off the heat until melted and spreadable.
Toast the bread, spread the rarebit thickly, and grill until bubbling and spotted.
Let it stand one minute so the cheese does not avalanche.
Serve with a little extra mustard at the table.

title: Smoked haddock kedgeree
description: Flaked smoked haddock, rice, egg and mild curry spice — a Boxing Day breakfast that uses the fishmonger's better leftovers.
notes: Undyed smoked haddock tastes cleaner than the bright yellow kind.
steps: Poach the haddock in water until it flakes, then lift it and cook the rice in the same liquor.
Boil the eggs to just firm yolks and peel them.
Melt butter with curry powder, fold in rice, then the fish in large flakes.
Quarter the eggs over the pan and finish with parsley.
Keep the fish in pieces; stirring hard turns kedgeree to mush.

title: Spiced Christmas porridge
description: Oats cooked with milk, cinnamon and a handful of raisins for a quiet Christmas-morning pan before the chaos.
notes: Use gluten-free oats if anyone at the table needs them.
steps: Combine oats, milk, raisins and cinnamon in a pan.
Cook on low, stirring, until the porridge is creamy and the raisins plump.
Sweeten with brown sugar off the heat so it does not catch.
Rest one minute; it thickens as it stands.
Serve with extra milk for children who like it looser.

title: Panettone eggy bread
description: Thick slices of leftover panettone soaked in egg and fried in butter until the cut candied peel caramelises.
notes: Stale panettone works better than very fresh, which soaks too fast.
steps: Beat eggs with milk and soak panettone slices briefly so they drink but do not collapse.
Fry in butter over medium heat until both sides are deep gold.
The sugar in the panettone browns fast; lower the heat if the butter darkens.
Dust with icing sugar and serve immediately.
A spoon of yogurt on the side cuts the sweetness.

title: Roast sprout breakfast hash
description: Leftover sprouts and potatoes chopped and fried with onion into a Boxing Day hash with crisp bits.
notes: Undercooked leftover sprouts crisp better than boiled-to-grey ones.
steps: Chop sprouts and potatoes into rough dice and slice the onion.
Soften onion in butter, then add potatoes and let them catch.
Fold in sprouts and salt, pressing the hash so more surface browns.
Flip in sections rather than stirring constantly.
Serve with cold ham or a fried egg.

title: Cranberry gin fizz
description: A sharp Christmas-eve long drink of gin, cranberry and sparkling water over ice with orange peel.
notes: Use unsweetened cranberry if you can; sweetened juice needs less.
steps: Fill tumblers with ice cubes.
Pour gin and cranberry juice over the ice and stir once.
Top with sparkling water so the drink stays bright, not syrupy.
Twist orange peel over each glass to spray the oils, then drop it in.
Do not make a jug hours ahead or the fizz dies.

title: Bread-sauce stuffed onions
description: Onion shells filled with clove-scented bread sauce crumbs and baked until the edges catch — a vegetarian nod to the classic sauce.
notes: Save the scooped onion to fold into stuffing.
steps: Halve the onions, parboil until just yielding, then scoop a nest in each half.
Warm milk with cloves, stir in breadcrumbs, butter and salt, and discard the cloves.
Fill the onion shells, dot with extra butter, and bake at 190°C until the tops brown.
The onion should be soft enough to cut with a spoon.
Serve as a side or a small vegetarian plate with greens.

title: Minted buttered peas
description: Frozen peas tossed with butter and mint — the cheapest green on a Christmas plate that still tastes deliberate.
notes: A pinch of sugar helps very starchy supermarket peas.
steps: Boil the peas in salted water until they float and turn bright, about four minutes.
Drain well so water does not dilute the butter.
Toss with butter and chopped mint off the heat.
Taste for salt; peas need more than you think.
Serve immediately; mint blacks if the pan sits on heat.

title: Thyme fondant potatoes
description: Potato cylinders browned in butter then braised in stock until the centres are spoon-tender — a smarter roast-potato cousin.
notes: Use a cutter if you want restaurant-neat sides; rustic barrels taste the same.
steps: Cut potatoes into even barrels about 4 cm tall and pat them dry.
Brown both cut faces in butter in an ovenproof pan.
Pour in stock to come halfway up, add thyme and salt, and transfer to a 190°C oven.
Cook until a knife meets no resistance and the tops are glazed.
Reduce any remaining stock to a syrup and spoon it over.

title: Sarmale in pickled cabbage
description: Pork and rice rolls tucked into pickled cabbage leaves and baked slowly under a lid of sauerkraut until the sauce turns silky.
notes: A smoked rib tucked among the rolls is traditional if you have one.
steps: Rinse very salty cabbage leaves, then mix pork with rinsed rice, grated onion, thyme and tomato paste.
Place a spoon of filling on each leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Line a pot with sauerkraut, pack the sarmale in layers, and cover with more sauerkraut and a little water.
Bake covered at 160°C for three hours until the rice is tender and the sauce tastes mellow.
Rest 20 minutes before serving with polenta or bread.

title: Cozonac braid
description: A Romanian Christmas sweet bread enriched with egg and butter, braided so the crumb stays feathery.
notes: A humid kitchen helps the dough stay extensible; do not add extra flour too soon.
steps: Warm milk, dissolve yeast and a spoon of sugar, then mix with flour, remaining sugar, eggs, vanilla and soft butter.
Knead until the dough is smooth and elastic; let it rise until doubled.
Divide, roll into ropes, braid, and set in a loaf tin for a second rise.
Brush with leftover egg and bake at 170°C until the loaf sounds hollow and the top is deep gold.
Cool on a rack before slicing so the crumb does not compress.

title: Piftie pork aspic
description: A jellied pork terrine set with garlic, sliced cold for Christmas Eve alongside bread and pickles.
notes: If the jelly is weak, reduce the liquor further before pouring.
steps: Cover trotters and shoulder with water, add bay and salt, and simmer four hours until the meat falls apart.
Lift the meat, shred it, and mix with crushed garlic and pepper.
Strain the liquor, reduce slightly, and pour it over the meat in a dish.
Chill overnight until the aspic is sliceable.
Serve cold with bread, horseradish or pickled peppers.

title: Salată de boeuf
description: A finely diced salad of root vegetables and beef bound with mayonnaise, decorated for the Christmas table.
notes: Vegetables must be cold before mixing or the mayonnaise splits.
steps: Simmer beef until tender; boil potato, carrot and parsley root separately until just done, then cool.
Dice meat, vegetables and gherkins into even small cubes.
Fold through enough mayonnaise to bind without turning the salad soupy.
Chill at least two hours, then mound and decorate with extra mayonnaise if you like a festive finish.
Taste for pickle brine; a spoon of it brightens a flat batch.

title: Ciorbă de perișoare
description: A sour meatball soup finished with lovage — a Romanian winter bowl that sits well before sarmale or as a light Christmas Eve supper.
notes: Bors brine can replace vinegar if you have it.
steps: Mix pork with egg, rinsed rice and salt; roll small meatballs.
Simmer diced carrot and parsley root in salted water until they begin to soften.
Poach the meatballs in the broth until they float and the rice inside is cooked.
Sharpen with vinegar and finish with chopped lovage off the heat.
The soup should taste sour-savoury, not like a stew.

title: Tochitură moldovenească
description: A Moldavian pork stew finished with wine and egg, served over polenta with a salty cheese crumble.
notes: Use a well-seasoned pan; the fond is the sauce.
steps: Brown pork cubes in lard until the edges catch, then add crushed garlic.
Pour in wine and simmer until the meat is tender and the sauce is reduced.
Cook polenta in salted water until thick.
Stir eggs into the pork off the heat so they just set in the sauce.
Serve the stew over polenta with crumbled telemea.

title: Sarmale de post
description: Lenten cabbage rolls stuffed with mushrooms, rice and onion, baked until the leaves are silk and the filling is savoury.
notes: A spoon of tomato paste in the water adds colour without meat.
steps: Chop mushrooms and onion finely and cook in oil until dry and browned.
Stir in rinsed rice, thyme and salt; cool the filling.
Roll in cabbage leaves and pack into a pot with a little water.
Bake covered at 160°C for two hours until the rice is cooked and the leaves are tender.
Rest 15 minutes; vegan sarmale need that pause to set.

title: Vin fiert
description: Romanian mulled wine with cinnamon, cloves and a slice of apple, kept below a boil for winter evenings.
notes: A cheap merlot-style wine is enough.
steps: Combine wine, apple slices, orange peel, cinnamon, cloves and sugar in a pan.
Heat until the surface shivers; hold there 12 minutes.
Taste and add sugar only if the wine is very dry.
Strain into glasses, returning a cinnamon stick for scent.
Do not boil; boiled vin fiert tastes cooked and thin.

title: Papanași
description: Fried cheese doughnuts with a smaller doughnut lid, served with sour cream and sour cherry jam.
notes: The cheese should be well drained or the dough drinks oil.
steps: Mash the cheese with eggs, sugar, baking powder and enough flour to make a soft dough.
Shape large rings and small balls, keeping the dough flour-dusted so it does not stick.
Fry in medium-hot oil until mahogany, turning once; drain on paper.
Stack a ring, a spoon of sour cream and jam, and the small doughnut as a lid.
Serve immediately while the crust is still crisp against the cream.

title: Gogoși with jam
description: Soft Romanian doughnuts fried until golden and rolled in sugar, split and filled with jam at the table.
notes: Keep oil around 170°C; too hot browns the outside before the crumb cooks.
steps: Make a yeast dough with flour, warm milk, butter, egg, yeast and a spoon of sugar; rise until puffy.
Roll to 1.5 cm, cut rounds, and rest 15 minutes.
Fry in oil that is hot enough to sizzle but not scorch, turning once.
Drain and toss in remaining sugar.
Serve with plum jam for spooning or filling.

title: Salată de icre
description: Carp or pike roe whipped with oil into a pale emulsion, finished with onion — a Christmas Eve fish starter.
notes: If the emulsion splits, beat a spoon of it into a fresh teaspoon of roe and oil, then return the rest.
steps: Rinse the roe if very salty and drain it well.
Beat the roe while dripping in oil as if making mayonnaise, until the mixture is pale and thick.
Fold in grated onion, lemon juice, salt and white pepper.
Chill 30 minutes so the emulsion firms.
Serve with bread and raw onion rings if the table likes extra bite.

title: Cozonac cu nucă
description: The walnut-swirl version of cozonac, with a dark filling of ground walnuts, cocoa and rum rolled through enriched dough.
notes: A slightly sticky filling swirls better than a dry one.
steps: Make an enriched yeast dough with flour, milk, eggs and butter; let it rise until doubled.
Grind walnuts and mix with cocoa, rum and enough sugar to make a spreadable paste.
Roll the dough thin, spread the walnut filling, and roll into a tight log; place in a tin to rise again.
Bake at 170°C until the loaf is browned and a skewer comes out clean of wet dough.
Cool completely before slicing to keep the swirl intact.

title: Ciorbă rădăuțeană
description: A garlic-sour chicken soup from Rădăuți, thickened with egg and sour cream, bright with vinegar.
notes: Boiling after the eggs go in will scramble the soup.
steps: Simmer chicken with carrot until the meat is tender; lift and shred it.
Beat eggs with sour cream and a ladle of hot broth, then return the liaison to the pan off the boil.
Add crushed garlic, vinegar and the shredded chicken.
Warm without boiling so the soup stays silky.
Finish with parsley and more garlic if the table wants it sharp.

title: Fasole bătută
description: White beans mashed with garlic and oil until creamy, topped with caramelised onion — a Lenten and Christmas Eve staple.
notes: Undercooked beans will never mash smooth.
steps: Soak beans overnight, then simmer until completely soft; drain, keeping a cup of liquor.
Mash beans with crushed garlic, salt and most of the oil, loosening with liquor until spreadable.
Fry onion in remaining oil until deep brown, then add paprika.
Spoon onion and oil over the bean mash.
Serve warm or room temperature with bread or next to sarmale de post.

title: Varză călită
description: Slow-cooked cabbage with paprika and a little tomato, sweet and silky enough to sit under roast pork.
notes: A pinch of caraway is welcome in Transylvania.
steps: Shred cabbage and onion.
Cook onion in oil, add paprika and tomato paste, then pile in cabbage and salt.
Cover and cook on low, stirring now and then, until the cabbage collapses and sweetens.
Uncover to evaporate extra liquid; you want a moist heap, not soup.
Reheats beautifully the next day.

title: Pomana porcului
description: A mixed pork fry of fresh cuts and offal served after the winter pig slaughter, still eaten as a rich Christmas main with polenta.
notes: Do not overcook the liver or it turns sandy.
steps: Cut meats into even pieces; soak kidney briefly if strong, then dry.
Brown shoulder in lard first, then add kidney, liver last so it stays pink inside.
Add onion and garlic and cook until the onion is soft and the pan juices are savoury.
Finish with parsley and plenty of black pepper.
Serve with polenta and pickles to cut the richness.

title: Winter stuffed peppers
description: Peppers filled with pork and rice, baked in a light tomato sauce — a family dish that stretches a small amount of meat.
notes: Undercooking the rice is the usual failure; test one pepper before serving.
steps: Mix pork with rinsed rice, grated onion and dill.
Fill the peppers loosely so the rice has room to swell.
Stand them in a dish, pour passata and a little water around, and cover.
Bake at 170°C until the rice is tender and the peppers collapse slightly.
Spoon the tomato juices over each pepper at the table.

title: Ciorbă de fasole
description: A sour bean soup with smoked meat optional, thickened by the beans themselves and finished with vinegar and parsley.
notes: Do not add vinegar until the beans are fully tender or they stay hard.
steps: Soak beans, then simmer with onion, carrot, bay and salt until creamy inside.
Mash a cup of beans back into the pot to thicken the broth.
Sharpen with vinegar and taste for salt.
Finish with parsley.
Serve with red onion and bread; smoked sausage can simmer in for a meat day.

title: Plăcintă cu mere
description: A rustic apple pie between two sheets of dough, scented with cinnamon — everyday Romanian baking that belongs on a winter table.
notes: Too much apple juice makes a soggy middle; squeeze the grate.
steps: Make a short dough with flour and butter, rest it, then divide in two.
Peel and grate the apples, squeeze lightly, and toss with sugar and cinnamon.
Line a tin with one sheet, pile in apples, cover with the second sheet, and brush with egg.
Bake at 180°C until the pastry is gold and the apples bubble at the edges.
Cool until just warm so slices hold.

title: Rasol de vită
description: Gently simmered beef with root vegetables, served with horseradish — a clear, honest winter main.
notes: A rolling boil toughens the brisket; keep it lazy.
steps: Cover brisket with water, bring slowly to a simmer, and skim.
Add onion, bay and salt; cook until the beef is tender, about two hours.
Add carrot and parsnip for the last 40 minutes so they do not collapse.
Slice the beef across the grain and serve in bowls with vegetables and broth.
Horseradish on the side is not optional if you can get it.

title: Friptură de porc la cuptor
description: A garlic-rubbed pork roast baked over onions until the fat bastes the meat and the onions turn into a sauce.
notes: Shoulder stays juicier than loin for this long roast.
steps: Crush garlic with salt and rub it all over the pork with pepper and thyme.
Set the joint on sliced onions in a roasting tin.
Roast at 170°C until the centre is 75°C and the onions have melted.
Rest 20 minutes, then slice and spoon onion juices over.
A splash of water in the tin halfway keeps the onions from scorching.

title: Salată de vinete
description: Charred aubergine mashed with oil and onion into a smoky spread for bread on Christmas Eve.
notes: Draining is the difference between salad and sludge.
steps: Roast whole aubergines until the skins blister and the flesh collapses.
Scoop the flesh, drain it in a sieve, then chop until almost a paste.
Beat in oil, grated onion, lemon and salt.
Chill so the spread firms and the smoke settles.
Serve with tomatoes or just bread.

title: Zacuscă de casă
description: A slow-cooked spread of roasted peppers, aubergine and onion, made ahead to open as a Christmas-eve jar.
notes: Low heat prevents catching; a heavy pan helps.
steps: Roast peppers and aubergines until charred; peel and chop.
Cook onion in oil until sweet, add tomato paste, then the chopped vegetables and salt.
Simmer, stirring often, until the zacuscă is thick and shiny, about an hour.
Cool and jar; the flavour rounds after a day.
Spread on bread as a starter or a Lenten meal.

title: Ciorbă de varză
description: A sour cabbage soup with optional smoked pork, the kind of bowl that warms a house after midnight church.
notes: Skip pork for a vegan Christmas Eve version.
steps: Rinse sauerkraut if it is extremely salty, then chop it.
Sweat onion and carrot, add paprika, sauerkraut, smoked pork and bay.
Cover with water and simmer until the cabbage is soft and the pork yields.
Taste; add a splash of brine if it is not sour enough.
Serve with bread and chilli if you like heat.

title: Cozonac cu rahat
description: Enriched Christmas bread rolled with cubes of rahat (lokum) that melt into scented pockets.
notes: Rose or lemon rahat both work; avoid chocolate-coated cubes.
steps: Make a rich yeast dough with flour, milk, eggs, butter, sugar and yeast; let it rise.
Dice rahat and toss it in a spoon of flour so the cubes stay separate.
Roll the dough, scatter rahat, and roll into a log for a second rise in a tin.
Bake at 170°C until golden and cooked through.
Cool before cutting so the rahat pockets set rather than tearing.

title: Piftie de pui
description: Chicken aspic set with garlic, a lighter piftie for tables that want the jelly without pork trotters.
notes: Wings and backs give more gelatine than breast alone.
steps: Simmer the chicken with carrot, bay and salt until the meat falls from the bones, about three hours.
Shred the meat, mix with crushed garlic and pepper, and pack into a dish.
Reduce the strained liquor until it looks sticky on a cold spoon, then pour over.
Chill overnight.
Slice and serve with bread; if it does not set, reduce more next time or add a second back bone to the pot.

title: Tochitură ardelenească
description: Transylvanian pork stew with sausage and a fried egg on polenta — distinct from the Moldavian wine-and-egg version.
notes: Smoked sausage is the Transylvanian signature here; do not skip it.
steps: Brown pork in lard, then add sliced sausage and garlic.
Simmer with a splash of water until the pork is tender and the pan juices are concentrated.
Cook polenta thick.
Fry eggs sunny-side so the yolks stay runny.
Plate polenta, stew, crumbled telemea and an egg per person.

title: Sarmale in grape leaves
description: Smaller rolls in vine leaves with pork, rice and dill, simmered in a lemony broth — a Dobrogea table variant.
notes: Blanch fresh leaves 30 seconds if you are not using jarred ones.
steps: Rinse grape leaves if brined; mix pork with rice, grated onion and dill.
Roll tightly into small cigars.
Pack in a pan, cover with water and lemon slices, and weight with a plate.
Simmer 90 minutes until the rice is cooked and the leaves are tender.
Serve with yogurt or sour cream if the table is not keeping a fast.

title: Orez cu lapte
description: Romanian rice pudding cooked slowly in milk until creamy, finished with lemon zest or jam.
notes: A heavy pan and patience prevent scorching.
steps: Rinse rice and combine with milk, salt and a strip of lemon zest.
Cook on the lowest heat, stirring often, until the grains are soft and the milk is thick.
Stir in sugar off the heat so it does not catch.
Rest five minutes; it thickens further.
Serve warm with extra zest or a spoon of jam.

title: Turtă dulce
description: Romanian honey-spice cookies, rolled thin and baked until they snap, often hung or stacked for Christmas.
notes: Do not overbake or the honey turns bitter.
steps: Warm honey with sugar, then mix into flour, cinnamon, baking soda and egg to a firm dough.
Chill 30 minutes, roll thin, and cut shapes.
Bake at 180°C until the edges darken and the centres look dry.
Cool on a rack; they crisp as they cool.
Store in a tin with a slice of apple if you want them slightly chewy later.

title: Clătite with jam
description: Thin Romanian pancakes rolled around jam — a last-minute dessert when cozonac is already gone.
notes: The first pancake is the pan's seasoning; the second is the real one.
steps: Whisk flour, milk, eggs and salt into a thin batter; rest 10 minutes.
Fry thin pancakes in a lightly buttered pan, swirling to coat.
Spread each clătite with apricot jam and roll.
Keep warm under a cloth so they do not dry.
Dust with sugar or serve as they are.

title: Magiun on walnut toast
description: Unsweetened plum magiun spread on toast with crushed walnuts — a Romanian winter breakfast that is barely a recipe and wholly useful.
notes: True magiun is just plums; if yours is very sweet, skip cinnamon sugar.
steps: Toast the bread until the edges crisp.
Spread magiun thickly; it is already concentrated, so you do not need much sugar.
Crush walnuts and scatter them over with a pinch of cinnamon.
Serve at once so the toast stays crunchy against the paste.
A spoon of magiun also belongs next to cheese on a savoury plate.

title: Ciorbă de pui
description: A straightforward sour chicken soup with vegetables, lighter than rădăuțeană and good on Christmas Eve before fish.
notes: A handful of noodles can go in for children.
steps: Cover chicken with water, add onion, carrot and celery, and simmer until the meat is tender.
Skim, then lift the chicken and shred it.
Return meat to the broth, sharpen with vinegar, and taste for salt.
Finish with parsley.
Serve with extra vinegar at the table; Romanian soups are personal that way.

title: Mămăligă with cheese and sour cream
description: Firm polenta turned out of the pot, sliced, and served with cheese and sour cream as a vegetarian main or a side to sarmale.
notes: Coarse polenta needs longer than instant; taste before you turn it out.
steps: Bring salted water to a boil and rain in polenta, whisking so it does not lump.
Cook, stirring, until the mass pulls from the sides of the pan.
Turn out onto a board and let a skin form so you can slice wedges.
Serve with crumbled telemea and sour cream.
Leftover slices fry well in butter the next morning.

title: Gogoși de post
description: Lenten doughnuts made without egg or milk, fried and rolled in sugar for Christmas Eve.
notes: A wetter dough fries lighter than a stiff one.
steps: Mix flour with yeast, sugar, salt, water and oil into a soft dough; rise until doubled.
Pat out and cut rounds; rest 15 minutes.
Fry in oil until both sides are gold.
Drain and toss in extra sugar.
Eat the same day; vegan doughnuts stale faster than enriched ones.

title: Salată de boeuf de post
description: The Lenten version of salată de boeuf, built from potatoes, carrots and pickles bound with a lean emulsion instead of meat.
notes: Keeping the dice small is what makes it feel like the original.
steps: Boil potato and carrot until just tender; cool completely.
Dice vegetables and gherkins evenly, then fold in peas.
Bind with vegan mayonnaise and salt.
Chill two hours so the cubes settle into a sliceable salad.
Decorate with extra peas or pickle stars if you are presenting it as the feast salad.

title: Panettone with candied orange
description: A tall, slow-risen Christmas bread with candied orange and raisins, baked in a paper case until the crumb is feathery and the crust bronze.
notes: A home kitchen will not match a 48-hour bakery loaf; this method still gives a light, buttery crumb.
steps: Dissolve yeast in a spoon of warm water, then mix a soft dough with flour, eggs, sugar and softened butter; knead until glossy.
Let it rise until doubled, then knead in candied orange peel and raisins so they scatter through the dough.
Shape into a tight boule, drop into a panettone case, and rise until the dough crests the paper.
Bake at 170°C until a skewer comes out clean and the crust is deep gold, tenting if it colours too fast.
Cool upside down suspended on skewers so the crumb does not collapse as it sets.

title: Tortellini in brodo
description: Meat-filled tortellini served in a clear capon or beef broth — the Emilian Christmas first course.
notes: A purchased broth is fine if you skim it well; cloudy soup hides the pasta.
steps: Make pasta dough with flour and eggs, rest it 30 minutes, then roll it very thin.
Chop pork and prosciutto finely, season with nutmeg and a spoon of parmesan, and place tiny mounds on the pasta.
Cut squares, fold into triangles, and wrap into tortellini around a fingertip.
Simmer the broth until it is clear and tasting of meat, then poach the tortellini in it until they float.
Serve in bowls with remaining parmesan; the pasta should swim, not sit in a thick stew.

title: Herb-roast capon
description: A capon roasted with rosemary, garlic and white wine until the skin is lacquered and the breast still moist.
notes: A large chicken stands in if capon is hard to find; shorten the time.
steps: Pat the capon dry, salt it inside and out, and stuff the cavity with garlic and rosemary.
Rub the skin with oil and roast at 180°C, pouring wine into the tin after 30 minutes.
Baste twice with the tin juices until the thickest thigh is 75°C.
Rest 25 minutes before carving so the white meat stays juicy.
Reduce the juices for a light pan sauce; capon does not need a heavy gravy.

title: Panforte di Siena
description: A dense Sienese round of nuts, honey and spice, baked just until set and dusted with icing sugar.
notes: It keeps weeks wrapped — make it in early December.
steps: Toast hazelnuts and almonds, then chop them coarsely with the candied peel.
Warm honey until fluid and mix with flour, cinnamon and the nuts.
Press into a lined shallow tin and bake at 150°C until the surface looks set but not dry.
Cool completely, then dust thickly with icing sugar.
Slice in thin wedges; panforte is a nibble, not a cake slice.

title: Mostaccioli al cioccolato
description: Southern Italian diamond biscuits spiced with clove, baked firm, then dipped in dark chocolate.
notes: A pinch of pepper is traditional in some Campanian houses.
steps: Mix flour, sugar, honey, egg and cloves into a stiff dough; rest 20 minutes.
Roll to 8 mm and cut diamonds.
Bake at 170°C until the edges firm and the centres look dry.
Cool, then dip each biscuit in melted dark chocolate and set on parchment.
Let the chocolate harden before stacking.

title: Vin brulé
description: Italian mulled wine with orange, cinnamon and a strip of lemon peel, served steaming from a saucepan after midnight mass.
notes: Piedmontese tables often use a Barbera; any fruity red works.
steps: Put wine, orange slices, lemon peel, cinnamon, cloves and sugar in a pan.
Heat until fragrant and steaming, never boiling.
Steep 10 minutes and taste for sugar.
Ladle into glasses through a strainer.
Keep warm at the back of the stove for late guests.

title: Pandoro with vanilla cream
description: Star-shaped pandoro sliced and layered with lightly sweetened cream — the easy Christmas dessert when you buy the loaf.
notes: A bought pandoro is traditional; the work is in the cream.
steps: Whip cream with icing sugar, vanilla and a pinch of salt to soft peaks.
Slice the pandoro horizontally into stars.
Reassemble with cream between layers, or serve slices with a spoon of cream beside.
Dust the top with extra icing sugar so it looks snowed on.
Fill just before serving or the crumb weeps.

title: Struffoli al miele
description: Tiny fried dough balls glued with warm honey into a wreath and scattered with coloured sprinkles.
notes: The balls must be small or the centre stays raw.
steps: Mix flour, eggs and oil into a dough, roll into ropes, and cut pea-sized pieces.
Fry in batches until gold; drain well.
Warm honey with lemon zest until fluid, then toss the struffoli so every ball is coated.
Mound into a ring on a plate and scatter sprinkles while the honey is tacky.
Set at room temperature; do not refrigerate or they harden like stones.

title: Cotechino with lentils
description: A rich pork cotechino sausage served over lentils for New Year luck, equally at home on a northern Christmas table.
notes: Precooked cotechino is widely sold; still simmer it to heat through evenly.
steps: Simmer cotechino gently in water according to its wrapping until cooked through; keep the liquor.
Cook lentils with onion, carrot, bay and oil until tender, loosening with a splash of sausage liquor.
Slice the cotechino thickly.
Spoon lentils onto plates and lay sausage on top.
The lentils should be moist, not soupy, so they catch the pork fat.

title: Baccalà mantecato
description: Salt cod beaten with oil into a snowy spread, served on polenta crostini for a Venetian Christmas Eve.
notes: The beating is the recipe; a mixer paddle saves your arm.
steps: Soak salt cod 24 hours, changing water, then poach until it flakes; remove bones and skin.
Beat the fish with garlic while dripping in oil until it turns pale and fluffy.
Season with white pepper and parsley.
Cook polenta, cool, slice and grill into crostini.
Spoon the baccalà onto the polenta while the spread is still cool.

title: Ricciarelli di Siena
description: Chewy almond diamonds from Siena, cracked on top and snowed with icing sugar.
notes: Resting before baking is what gives the classic cracked crust.
steps: Mix ground almonds with most of the icing sugar, lemon zest and almond extract.
Whip egg whites to soft peaks and fold in to a sticky dough.
Shape diamonds with floury hands, roll in remaining sugar, and rest an hour so a skin forms.
Bake at 160°C until the tops crack but the insides stay moist.
Cool on the tray; they firm as they sit.

title: Panpepato
description: A peppered Christmas cake of nuts, chocolate and spice, denser and darker than panforte.
notes: It should taste warm-spicy, not like a steak pepper crust.
steps: Chop nuts and chocolate; mix with flour, pepper and cinnamon.
Warm honey and stir it through until the mass holds.
Shape into a small round on parchment.
Bake at 150°C until set at the edge but still slightly soft in the middle.
Cool, then wrap; the pepper blooms after a day.

title: Cappelletti in brodo
description: Hat-shaped pasta filled with cheese, cooked in capon broth — a Romagna Christmas cousin of tortellini.
notes: Vegetarian tables can use a rich vegetable broth; it will not be the same but it works.
steps: Make egg pasta and rest it.
Mix ricotta, parmesan and nutmeg into a firm filling.
Cut pasta squares, add filling, and fold into little hats, sealing well.
Bring capon broth to a gentle simmer and cook the cappelletti until they float and the pasta is tender.
Serve in the broth with more parmesan.

title: Zampone with lentils
description: A stuffed pig's trotter simmered until the skin is gelatinous, sliced over lentils for a feast plate.
notes: Buy zampone already prepared unless you have a butcher who stuffs them.
steps: Simmer the zampone very gently with bay until a knife slides through the skin, often two hours.
Cook lentils separately with onion, carrot and salt until just tender.
Slice the zampone thickly so each piece has skin, stuffing and jelly.
Spoon lentils onto a platter and overlap the slices.
Moisten with a little cooking liquor so nothing looks dry.

title: Insalata di mare
description: A lemony salad of mixed seafood for the Southern Christmas Eve fish table.
notes: Do not boil squid hard or it turns to rubber bands.
steps: Steam mussels until they open; poach squid and prawns in the same liquor until just opaque.
Cool the seafood and cut squid into rings.
Dress with oil, lemon juice and parsley while still slightly warm so the dressing soaks in.
Chill 30 minutes, then taste for salt and lemon.
Serve as a starter, not buried under mayonnaise.

title: Soft torrone
description: A chewy almond nougat set between wafer papers, cut into bars for the Christmas sweet box.
notes: A sugar thermometer to 120°C keeps the texture chewy rather than rock-hard.
steps: Toast almonds until they smell sweet.
Cook honey and sugar to a thick bubble, then fold into stiff egg whites to make a glossy nougat.
Stir in almonds and spread between sheets of wafer paper.
Press, cool, and cut into bars with an oiled knife.
Store airtight; humidity turns nougat sticky.

title: Festive lasagne al forno
description: Layered pasta with ragù and béchamel, baked until the corners crisp — a northern Italian Christmas lunch alternative to broth.
notes: Fresh pasta needs no pre-boil if the sauces are moist.
steps: Brown beef with onion and tomato paste into a thick ragù; simmer 30 minutes.
Make béchamel with butter-flour if needed, or flour cooked in a little fat, then milk; season.
Layer pasta, ragù, béchamel and parmesan in a dish.
Bake at 180°C until bubbling and spotted brown.
Rest 15 minutes so slices hold.

title: Bollito misto
description: A mixed boiled meat platter with salsa verde — a Piedmontese feast for a crowd.
notes: This is a timing exercise more than a single pot; start the brisket first.
steps: Simmer brisket with onion and carrot until tender, skimming often.
Cook cotechino and chicken in separate pots so their timings do not fight.
Slice all the meats and arrange on a hot platter with the vegetables.
Chop parsley into a sharp oil-and-garlic green sauce and serve alongside.
Keep a jug of broth on the table to moisten plates.

title: Porchetta with fennel
description: Pork belly rolled around loin with fennel, rosemary and garlic, roasted until the skin crackles.
notes: Dry the skin overnight in the fridge for better crackling.
steps: Crush fennel, garlic, rosemary and salt into a paste and rub it over the loin.
Wrap the belly around the loin, skin out, and tie tightly.
Roast at 160°C until the meat is tender, then blast at 230°C to crackle the skin.
Rest 20 minutes before slicing through the string.
Each slice should show a pinwheel of herb paste.

title: Amaretti morbidi
description: Soft almond cookies with cracked sugar tops, eaten with coffee after a long lunch.
notes: Do not overbake; dry amaretti are a different biscuit.
steps: Mix ground almonds and sugar, then fold in whipped egg whites and almond extract.
Roll balls, coat in icing sugar, and space on a tray.
Bake at 170°C until the tops crack and the bottoms barely colour.
Cool on the tray so the insides stay chewy.
They keep a week in a tin.

title: Panettone gastronomico
description: A savoury panettone split into layers and filled with cold cuts and cheese for an aperitivo centrepiece.
notes: Use a plain unsweetened panettone; the dessert loaf fights the ham.
steps: Slice the panettone horizontally into even layers.
Butter each layer lightly so the fillings grip.
Add prosciutto, provolone and rocket in separate layers so flavours stay distinct.
Reassemble, wrap tightly, and chill 30 minutes.
Cut into wedges like a cake.

title: Cartellate with vincotto
description: Ribbons of fried pastry coiled into roses and soaked in cooked grape syrup.
notes: Honey stands in for vincotto if needed.
steps: Mix flour with oil and wine into a firm dough; rest 30 minutes.
Roll thin, cut ribbons, pinch into rose coils, and rest so they dry slightly.
Fry until blistered and gold; drain.
Warm vincotto with cinnamon and dip or drizzle the cartellate.
Leave to soak an hour so the syrup reaches the folds.

title: Pangiallo
description: A Roman winter cake of dried fruit and nuts with a yellow saffron glaze, baked as a small dome.
notes: The saffron is for colour as much as flavour.
steps: Chop figs and nuts, mix with honey and flour into a stiff mass.
Shape into a small dome on parchment.
Brush with saffron steeped in a spoon of warm water.
Bake at 160°C until the outside firms.
Cool and slice thinly; it is rich.

title: Cavallucci
description: Soft Sienese cookies with walnuts, candied peel and anise, baked pale and slightly chewy.
notes: A drop of water on the dough helps if it crumbles.
steps: Warm honey and sugar, then mix into flour with chopped walnuts, peel and anise.
Shape into small ovals with floured hands.
Bake at 170°C until the bottoms just colour; the tops stay pale.
Cool on a rack; they soften in a tin after a day, which is correct.
Do not expect a snap; cavallucci are meant to be dense.

title: Baci di dama
description: Hazelnut biscuits sandwiched with chocolate — Piedmontese 'lady's kisses' for the sweet tray.
notes: Equal-sized balls matter more than perfect roundness.
steps: Grind toasted hazelnuts and mix with flour, butter and sugar into a dough.
Roll small balls, flatten slightly, and bake at 160°C until the edges colour.
Cool completely.
Sandwich pairs with melted dark chocolate and let them set.
Store cool so the chocolate does not smear.

title: Brodo di cappone
description: A clear capon broth that is both the cooking medium for tortellini and a restorative cup on its own.
notes: Chicken carcasses work; add a few wings for body.
steps: Cover the carcass and vegetables with cold water, add bay and salt, and bring slowly to a shiver.
Skim thoroughly in the first 20 minutes.
Simmer three hours without boiling so the broth stays clear.
Strain through cloth and cool; lift fat if you want a cleaner cup.
Reheat gently to serve in cups or to cook pasta.

title: Vitello tonnato for Christmas Eve
description: Poached veal sliced thin and coated in a tuna-caper sauce, served cold — a Piedmontese make-ahead starter.
notes: Pork loin is a common stand-in where veal is scarce.
steps: Poach the veal gently with a little salt until just cooked through; cool in the liquor.
Blend tuna, yolks, capers, oil and lemon into a smooth sauce.
Slice the veal thinly across the grain.
Blanket the slices with sauce and chill at least two hours.
Serve from the fridge, not warm; this is a cold plate.

title: Seadas with honey
description: Sardinian fried pastries filled with warm cheese, drizzled with honey — a festive sweet that is not panettone.
notes: Pecorino that melts is traditional; mozzarella is a poor swap.
steps: Make a firm dough with flour, oil, salt and water; rest it.
Roll thin, cut rounds, and sandwich lemon-zested cheese between two rounds, sealing well.
Fry until blistered and gold.
Drizzle with honey while hot so it soaks the pastry.
Serve immediately; the cheese should stretch.

title: Saffron risotto for the feast
description: Milanese saffron risotto served beside roast meats on a northern Christmas table, stirred until the rice is all'onda.
notes: Use proper saffron threads, not yellow colouring.
steps: Soften onion in half the butter, add rice, and toast until the grains look glassy.
Add stock ladle by ladle, stirring, with saffron steeped in a cup of the stock.
When the rice is tender but still has bite, beat in remaining butter and parmesan.
The risotto should flow in a wave when you tilt the pan.
Serve at once; it tightens as it sits.

title: Fried eel for Christmas Eve
description: Pieces of eel floured and fried until the skin crisps — a Roman Capitoline Christmas Eve fish.
notes: If eel is unavailable, use firm chunks of monkfish for a similar fry, though it is not the same dish.
steps: Ask the fishmonger to clean the eel; cut it into 5 cm pieces and pat dry.
Season with salt and dust with flour, shaking off the excess.
Fry in olive oil until the skin is crisp and the flesh pulls from the bone.
Drain on paper and serve with lemon.
Work in batches so the oil stays hot.

title: Bûche de Noël cacao
description: A cocoa sponge rolled around chocolate buttercream, scored to look like bark, with a dusting of sugar snow.
notes: Roll while warm or the sponge will crack later.
steps: Whip eggs and sugar until thick, fold in flour and cocoa, and bake a thin sponge at 190°C for about 10 minutes.
Turn onto a sugared cloth and roll while warm, then cool so the cake remembers the spiral.
Melt chocolate, beat with butter into a buttercream, unroll the sponge, spread, and roll again.
Coat the outside, drag a fork to mimic bark, and dust with icing sugar.
Chill 30 minutes before slicing with a hot knife.

title: Oysters with mignonette
description: Cold oysters opened to order and served with a shallot-vinegar mignonette for réveillon.
notes: Keep oysters refrigerated and serve within hours of opening.
steps: Chop shallots finely and soak them in vinegar with pepper to make mignonette.
Scrub the oysters and open them over a bowl to catch liquor, leaving them on the half shell.
Arrange on ice so they stay cold and level.
Spoon a little mignonette on each oyster at the table, with lemon wedges aside.
Discard any oyster that does not smell of the sea or whose shell was open before you shucked it.

title: Dinde aux marrons
description: A French Christmas turkey stuffed with chestnuts and sausage, roasted until the skin is lacquered.
notes: Chestnuts should stay whole in the stuffing, not mashed.
steps: Mix chestnuts with sausage meat, chopped onion and thyme for a loose stuffing.
Season the turkey, pack the stuffing into the cavity without ramming it, and truss.
Roast at 160°C, basting with wine and tin juices, until the thigh is 75°C.
Rest 30 minutes; spoon stuffing out with a ladle so it stays in chunks.
Deglaze the tin for a light jus rather than a floury gravy.

title: Gratin dauphinois
description: Thinly sliced potatoes baked in garlic cream until the top browns and the interior is satiny.
notes: Waxy potatoes hold their slices; floury ones collapse into mash.
steps: Rub a dish with garlic and butter.
Slice potatoes thinly, layer with salt, and pour over cream mixed with milk and remaining garlic.
Dot with butter and bake at 160°C until a knife meets no resistance and the top is spotted gold.
Rest 10 minutes so the cream sets enough to spoon.
Do not add cheese if you want the Dauphiné version; the cream is the point.

title: Vin chaud
description: Alsatian hot wine with orange, cinnamon and honey, sold at markets and easy to make in a single pan.
notes: Honey instead of white sugar is the Alsatian habit in this version.
steps: Warm wine with orange slices, cinnamon, star anise, cloves and honey.
Keep it below a boil for 15 minutes.
Taste; honey sweetness should not hide the wine.
Strain into thick glasses.
A strip of orange peel as garnish is enough.

title: Smoked salmon on blinis
description: Small buckwheat blinis topped with crème fraîche and smoked salmon for a réveillon nibble.
notes: Bought blinis are acceptable when the salmon is excellent.
steps: Whisk flours with eggs and milk into a thick batter; rest 20 minutes.
Fry small blinis in a lightly greased pan until bubbles set, then flip.
Cool slightly so the crème fraîche does not melt off.
Top each with crème fraîche and a fold of smoked salmon.
Serve at room temperature within an hour of assembling.

title: Chapon farci aux morilles
description: A capon stuffed with cream-soaked morels, roasted slowly so the mushroom perfume reaches the meat.
notes: Rinse soaked morels well; grit ruins the luxury.
steps: Soak morels, then cook them with shallot in butter and cream until the sauce clings.
Season the capon and spoon the cooled morel stuffing into the cavity.
Roast at 170°C until the thigh is cooked through, basting once or twice.
Rest 25 minutes, then carve and serve stuffing beside the slices.
Reduce any tin juices with a spoon of soaking liquor for a dark jus.

title: Boudin blanc with apples
description: White pudding sausages browned gently and served with caramelised apple — a réveillon plate that needs little work.
notes: Buy boudin blanc from a butcher; cheap ones are pasty.
steps: Brown the boudin blanc in butter over medium heat, turning until the skins are gold; do not prick them.
Quarter apples, add to the pan with sugar, and cook until the cut faces caramelise.
Season with a pinch of salt to keep the apples from tasting like dessert only.
Serve the sausages on the apples with pan juices.
Keep the heat moderate or the delicate filling splits.

title: Soupe à l'oignon gratinée
description: Deeply browned onion soup under a lid of bread and melted cheese, for a late cold réveillon.
notes: Patience on the onions is the whole recipe.
steps: Cook onions in butter until they are mahogany, 25 minutes at least.
Deglaze with wine, add stock, and simmer 20 minutes.
Ladle into bowls, float toasted baguette, and cover with grated gruyère.
Grill until the cheese bubbles and spots.
Warn diners the bowls are volcanic.

title: Confit de canard
description: Duck legs cooked slowly in their fat until the meat yields, then crisped in a hot pan.
notes: Confit keeps weeks under fat in the fridge.
steps: Salt duck legs with thyme and garlic and cure overnight.
Rinse lightly, then submerge in duck fat and cook at 140°C until the meat is spoon-tender.
Cool in the fat if making ahead.
To serve, lift and crisp the skin in a hot pan or under a grill.
Save the fat for potatoes.

title: Pain d'épices
description: A honey spice loaf from Dijon, sliced thin for breakfast or foie-gras toasts, here served as a simple cake.
notes: Rye flour is traditional; all wheat makes a different cake.
steps: Warm honey with milk, then mix into rye flour, spice, baking soda and egg.
Pour into a lined loaf tin.
Bake at 160°C until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool, wrap, and wait a day; the crumb moistens as it sits.
Slice thinly; it is dense on purpose.

title: Galette des rois
description: Puff pastry filled with almond cream, baked for Epiphany and often for the whole Christmas season.
notes: Hide a fève if you are playing the king game; warn guests.
steps: Beat butter, sugar, almonds, almond extract and one egg into frangipane.
Lay one pastry round, spread filling, leaving a border, and cover with the second round.
Seal, scallop the edge, egg-wash, and score a sunburst without cutting through.
Bake at 190°C until puffed and deep gold.
Cool slightly so the almond cream sets when sliced.

title: Tarte Tatin
description: Apples caramelised under pastry, inverted so the fruit sits glossy on top.
notes: Use apples that hold shape; Bramley turns to fluff.
steps: Cook sugar and butter in an ovenproof pan until you have an amber caramel; add a pinch of salt.
Pack peeled apple halves tightly in the caramel and cook until they start to soften.
Cover with puff pastry, tucked in at the edges.
Bake at 190°C until the pastry is cooked through.
Wait three minutes, then invert onto a plate while the caramel is still fluid.

title: Honey madeleines
description: Shell-shaped sponge cakes with honey, baked in a hot tin so they grow a hump.
notes: A hot oven and cold batter make the hump.
steps: Brown the butter lightly, then mix with eggs, sugar, honey, flour and baking powder.
Chill the batter 30 minutes.
