Beat leftover porridge with eggs, sugar and cinnamon.
Pour in and bake at 180°C until the filling is set and the pastry gold.
Cool until just warm.
Serve with leftover cherry sauce if you have risalamande remnants.

title: Fennel-cured salmon
description: A gravlax relative cured with fennel fronds instead of only dill, for a second fish plate.
notes: Do not serve both cures unlabeled; they look the same in photographs.
steps: Crush fennel seeds with salt and sugar, rub over salmon, and pack with fennel fronds.
Cure 36 hours weighted in the fridge, turning once.
Pat dry and slice thinly.
The flavour should be anise-green, not identical to dill gravlax.
Serve with rye and lemon.

title: Barley cream porridge
description: A weekday-style barley porridge with milk, for a quieter Norwegian Christmas breakfast than rømmegrøt.
notes: Pearl barley needs patience; do not rush with high heat.
steps: Simmer barley in milk with salt until the grains are tender and the porridge is creamy.
Stir in butter and sugar.
Rest two minutes.
Serve in bowls; it thickens as it stands.
A sprinkle of cinnamon is optional.

title: Glazed carrots for lamb ribs
description: Carrots glazed with a little of the pinnekjøtt steaming liquor and butter, for colour on a brown plate.
notes: A small side, not a second mash.
steps: Boil carrots until just tender; drain.
Glaze in butter, sugar and a spoon of steaming liquor.
Taste for salt; the liquor may already be plenty.
They should shine, not sit in syrup.
Skip the liquor if it is fiercely salty.

title: Töltött káposzta
description: Hungarian stuffed cabbage in sauerkraut with paprika and sour cream — distinct from Romanian sarmale by the paprika-sour cream finish and from Polish gołąbki by the pickled leaf.
notes: Smoked knuckle in the pot is traditional if you have one.
steps: Mix pork with rice, onion and most of the paprika.
Roll in sauerkraut leaves and nestle in more chopped sauerkraut.
Simmer covered 2 hours until the rice is tender and the sauce is brick-red.
Stir remaining paprika into sour cream and spoon over at the table.
The paprika should be sweet and present, not an afterthought.

title: Mákos bejgli
description: A Hungarian Christmas roll with a dense poppy-seed filling, glazed so the crust cracks in a mosaic.
notes: The crackled glaze is a bejgli signature; do not tent with foil too early.
steps: Make a rich dough with flour, butter and milk; rest chilled.
Grind poppy seeds and cook with sugar and a little milk into a thick filling; cool.
Roll dough, spread filling, roll tightly, and rest so the surface dries.
Brush with egg, pierce, and bake at 180°C until the crust is gold and crackled.
Cool before slicing thin.

title: Diós bejgli
description: The walnut-filled sister of mákos bejgli, same cracked crust, darker swirl.
notes: Many Hungarian tables serve both poppy and walnut rolls.
steps: Make the same rich dough as for poppy bejgli and chill it.
Grind walnuts with sugar into a thick paste loosened with a spoon of milk.
Roll, fill, roll, egg-wash, and bake at 180°C until crackled and cooked through.
Cool completely.
Slice with a serrated knife so the walnut spiral stays tight.

title: Halászlé
description: A brick-red river-fish soup heavy with paprika, often the Christmas Eve fish course in Hungary.
notes: Carp plus a firmer fish makes a better pot than carp alone.
steps: Cook onion until soft, take off the heat, and stir in paprika so it does not burn.
Add water, tomato, pepper and fish heads or trimmings; simmer into a stock, then strain.
Poach fish fillets in the red broth until just done.
The soup should be fiery-coloured and savoury.
Serve with bread, not cream.

title: Rakott krumpli
description: Layered potatoes with egg, sausage and sour cream, baked until the top catches — a Hungarian family bake.
notes: Skip sausage for a vegetarian bake and add extra egg.
steps: Boil potatoes and eggs; slice both.
Layer potatoes, egg, sausage and sour cream in a buttered dish, salting as you go.
Finish with sour cream and bake at 190°C until bubbling and spotted.
Rest 10 minutes.
It should slice into messy squares, not a neat gratin tower.

title: Palacsinta with walnut filling
description: Thin Hungarian pancakes rolled around a walnut-sugar filling, a Christmas sweet when bejgli is already sliced.
notes: Thinner than British pancakes; swirl the pan.
steps: Whisk a thin batter from flour, milk and eggs; rest 10 minutes.
Fry thin pancakes in a lightly buttered pan.
Mix ground walnuts with sugar and a spoon of milk into a spreadable filling.
Roll each palacsinta around the filling.
Serve warm; a chocolate drizzle is allowed but not required.

title: Kürtőskalács
description: Chimney cake dough wrapped around a spit or bottle, rolled in sugar, and baked until the sugar caramelises.
notes: Walnut or cinnamon sugar on the outside are common finishes.
steps: Make a soft yeast dough; rise until puffy.
Roll strips and wrap them around a greased cylinder, stretching slightly.
Brush with butter, roll in sugar, and bake at 200°C, turning, until caramelised.
Slide off and serve warm.
A bottle wrapped in foil works if you lack a spit.

title: Kocsonya
description: Hungarian pork aspic with garlic, set in bowls and eaten cold — a winter feast starter.
notes: Related to Romanian piftie but usually served in individual bowls with paprika dust.
steps: Simmer trotters and shoulder with bay and salt until the meat falls apart, about 3 hours.
Shred meat, mix with crushed garlic, and divide among bowls.
Pour strained liquor over and chill overnight.
Serve cold with paprika and vinegar on the table.
If it does not set, reduce the liquor further next time.

title: Mákos guba
description: Stale bread rolls soaked in milk, baked with ground poppy and sugar — a thrifty Hungarian Christmas pudding.
notes: Day-old rolls work better than sandwich bread.
steps: Slice rolls and pack in a buttered dish.
Pour over milk and rest until the bread drinks.
Scatter ground poppy mixed with sugar, dot with butter, and bake at 180°C until the top catches.
Serve it warm, not piping, so the flavours stay clear.
It should be custardy inside, toasted on top.

title: Gulyásleves
description: A proper Hungarian goulash soup with beef, potato and paprika, for a winter evening that is not the stuffed-cabbage feast.
notes: Do not add flour; body comes from onion and time.
steps: Brown onion, take off heat, stir in paprika, then add beef and water.
Simmer until the beef is tender, about an hour.
Add potato and carrot and cook until they soften.
The result is a soup, not a thick stew.
Serve with bread and csipetke pinches of dough if you like.

title: Lángos
description: Fried potato-yeast flatbreads rubbed with garlic and sour cream, a market snack that children claim at Christmas fairs.
notes: Cheese on top is common; keep it optional for a lighter version.
steps: Mix mashed potato with flour, yeast, salt and water into a soft dough; rise 45 minutes.
Stretch rounds and fry in oil until blistered and gold.
Rub with garlic and top with sour cream.
Eat immediately.
They go leathery if they wait.

title: Lencsefőzelék
description: A thick lentil stew eaten on New Year's Day for luck, welcome on any winter table.
notes: New Year luck lore is optional; the stew is good regardless.
steps: Cook lentils with onion until very soft.
Make a light roux with butter and flour, loosen with lentil liquor, and stir back into the pot.
Sharpen with vinegar and salt.
The főzelék should be thick enough to stand a spoon.
Serve with a fried egg or just bread.

title: Smažený kapr
description: Czech Christmas Eve fried carp, breaded and fried, served with potato salad.
notes: A scale in the wallet is the folk luck charm; skip it if you like.
steps: Cut carp into portions, salt, then flour, egg and breadcrumb.
Fry in oil until the crumb is gold and the fish flakes.
Drain the fried pieces on paper so the crust stays crisp rather than soggy.
Serve with bramborový salát.
Keep the oil hot so the crust does not soak.

title: Bramborový salát
description: Czech potato salad with carrot, pea, pickle and mayonnaise — the required partner to fried carp.
notes: Make it in the morning so the flavours marry.
steps: Boil potatoes and carrots until just tender; cool and dice.
Dice pickles and onion finely.
Fold everything with mayonnaise and peas.
Chill at least two hours.
It should be creamy but still show distinct cubes.

title: Vanilkové rohlíčky
description: Czech vanilla crescents of ground walnuts, rolled in vanilla sugar while warm.
notes: Walnuts are the Czech habit; almonds make a different crescent.
steps: Mix flour, butter, walnuts and icing sugar into a dough; chill 30 minutes.
Shape small crescents and bake at 170°C until the undersides just colour.
Roll in vanilla sugar while warm.
Cool completely.
They should be sandy and fragile, not brown like shortbread overbaked.

title: Vánočka
description: A braided Czech Christmas bread with raisins and almonds, sliced for breakfast with butter.
notes: A tea towel over the loaf while cooling keeps the crust tender.
steps: Make an enriched dough; knead in raisins.
Braid in two tiers (four-strand base, three-strand top) and rise until puffy.
Brush with egg, scatter almonds, and bake at 170°C until gold and cooked through.
Cool before slicing.
The braid should stay defined, not melt into a loaf.

title: Svíčková
description: Beef sirloin braised with root vegetables, puréed into a sweet-sour cream sauce, served with dumplings and cranberry.
notes: A Christmas lunch main when the Eve was fish.
steps: Brown the beef, then braise with carrot, celeriac and onion until tender.
Lift the meat; purée the vegetables with the liquor, then add cream, vinegar and sugar.
The sauce should be apricot-coloured and silky.
Slice the beef and nap with sauce.
Serve with bread dumplings and a spoon of cranberry.

title: Medovník
description: A many-layered honey cake stacked with sour-cream filling, best after a night in the fridge.
notes: The wait is mandatory; same-day medovník is crunchy in the wrong way.
steps: Make a honey dough with flour, honey, eggs and soda; roll several thin rounds and bake them pale.
Sweeten sour cream for the filling.
Stack layers with filling, coating the outside.
Chill overnight so the honey sheets soften.
Slice like a cake the next day.

title: Linecké cukroví
description: Linzer-style sandwich cookies of butter dough with jam windows, a Czech Christmas tin essential.
notes: Currant or raspberry jam is traditional.
steps: Make a short dough, chill, and roll.
Cut pairs, cutting a small window in half of them.
Bake at 170°C until just gold.
Sandwich with jam and dust with icing sugar.
Fill when cool so the jam does not melt out.

title: Rumové kuličky
description: No-bake Czech rum balls of biscuit crumb, cocoa and rum, rolled in sprinkles.
notes: A Czech cookie-plate cousin of German rumkugeln, using biscuit crumb.
steps: Crush biscuits and mix with melted butter, cocoa and rum.
Chill until scoopable, then roll balls.
Coat in sprinkles.
Chill the balls until they set firm enough to pile without smearing.
They should smell of rum without being wet.

title: Bramboráky
description: Garlic-heavy Czech potato pancakes, thinner and more savoury than German puffers.
notes: Marjoram is a common extra if you have it.
steps: Grate potatoes, squeeze dry, and mix with crushed garlic, egg, flour and salt.
Fry thin pancakes until both sides are crisp.
The garlic should be loud.
Drain the fried pieces on paper so the crust stays crisp rather than soggy.
Serve with soup or as a snack.

title: Rybí polévka
description: Czech fish soup from carp heads and vegetables, the Christmas Eve first course before fried carp.
notes: Root vegetables should flavour, not turn the soup into a stew.
steps: Simmer carp heads with vegetables and salt, skimming, until you have a tasty stock, about 45 minutes.
Strain, pick any meat, and return it to the broth.
Finish with parsley.
Serve in cups before the fried fish.
Do not boil hard or the soup clouds.

title: Banitsa
description: Filo coiled or layered with eggs and sirene cheese, a Bulgarian Christmas and New Year breakfast pie.
notes: Feta stands in for sirene.
steps: Beat eggs with yogurt, soda and crumbled sirene.
Brush filo with butter, add filling, and coil or layer in a round tin.
Bake at 180°C until the pastry is deep gold and the cheese is set.
Rest 10 minutes.
Serve warm; lucky charms go in at New Year if you play that game.

title: Bulgarian sarmi
description: Cabbage rolls with rice, mint and sometimes minced meat, often meatless on Christmas Eve — distinct from Romanian sarmale by mint and a lighter filling.
notes: Meat versions exist; this Eve version stays meatless.
steps: Cook onion in oil, add rice, mint and salt, and cool the filling slightly.
Roll in cabbage leaves and pack in a pot with water.
Simmer until the rice is tender, about 90 minutes.
The filling is mostly rice; it should not taste like a meatball.
Serve with yogurt if the fast allows.

title: Bob chorba
description: A Bulgarian bean soup with mint and paprika, a Lenten Christmas Eve bowl.
notes: Do not skip mint; without it this is just bean soup.
steps: Soak beans, then simmer with onion and carrot until creamy.
Fry paprika briefly in oil and stir it in with mint.
The soup should taste minty and earthy.
Mash a few beans to thicken.
Serve with bread and pickled peppers.

title: Shopska salad
description: Tomato, cucumber and sirene salad, still served in winter with hothouse vegetables as a sharp Bulgarian side.
notes: Salt the tomatoes lightly; sirene is already salty.
steps: Chop tomato, cucumber and onion into even pieces.
Dress with oil and parsley.
Grate sirene over the top rather than mixing it in.
Serve at once while the vegetables are still bright and crisp.
The cheese should look like a snow cap.

title: Kozunak
description: Bulgarian Easter-and-Christmas enriched bread, braided, close to Romanian cozonac but often with a simpler crumb.
notes: Rum-soaked raisins are a common extra.
steps: Make a rich yeast dough with flour, milk, butter, eggs, sugar, yeast and vanilla; knead until elastic.
Rise, braid, and rise again.
Brush with egg and bake at 170°C until the loaf sounds hollow.
Cool the loaf on a rack so the crumb does not steam and compact.
Slice the next day for a neater crumb.

title: Tikvenik
description: A pumpkin filo strudel with sugar and cinnamon, a Bulgarian winter sweet.
notes: Butternut works if pumpkin is watery.
steps: Grate pumpkin, squeeze lightly, and toss with sugar, cinnamon and chopped walnuts.
Layer filo brushed with oil, add filling, and roll.
Bake at 180°C until the pastry is crisp and the pumpkin tender.
Cool slightly before slicing.
The filling should not flood the filo; squeeze the pumpkin.

title: Kapama
description: A layered Christmas pot of sauerkraut, rice, and mixed meats baked slowly until the house smells of paprika and cabbage.
notes: A festive mountain dish; timings assume a tight lid.
steps: Layer sauerkraut, rinsed rice, meats, onion and paprika in a heavy pot.
Add a little water, cover tightly, and bake at 160°C for three hours.
Do not stir; let the layers cook down.
Rest 20 minutes before serving from the pot.
The rice should be tender and stained with cabbage juices.

title: Serbian sarma
description: Pickled-cabbage rolls with pork and rice, often with smoked meat in the pot — a Serbian Christmas day dish distinct from the Romanian and Hungarian cousins by smoked ribs and a browner sauce.
notes: Smoked ribs in the pot are the Serbian tell in this version.
steps: Mix pork with rice, onion and paprika.
Roll in leaves, pack with smoked ribs among them, and cover with water.
Simmer or bake 2.5 hours until the rice is done and the sauce is rich.
Rest 15 minutes.
Serve with bread; yogurt is optional.

title: Česnica
description: A Serbian Christmas bread with a coin hidden inside, broken rather than cut at the table.
notes: The coin must be clean and well wrapped.
steps: Make a simple enriched dough; rise until doubled.
Wrap a clean coin in foil, bury it in the dough, and shape a round loaf.
Rise again and bake at 180°C until gold.
Cool, then break by hand at the table.
Warn everyone about the coin.

title: Vanilice
description: Tiny Serbian sandwich cookies with jam, rolled in vanilla sugar, meltingly short.
notes: Apricot jam is common; rose jam is a treat.
steps: Mix flour, butter, walnuts and icing sugar into a dough; chill.
Cut small rounds, bake at 160°C until barely coloured.
Sandwich with jam and roll in vanilla sugar.
They should be bite-size.
Store in a tin; they soften slightly.

title: Pečena prasetina
description: Roast suckling pig or a pork shoulder treated like one, with crackling skin, a Serbian Christmas spit-roast translated to the oven.
notes: True spit pig is party food; this oven shoulder is the home version.
steps: Score the skin, rub with salt, garlic, oil and rosemary, and rest overnight if you can.
Roast at 160°C, pouring beer into the tin once, until the meat yields.
Blast the skin at high heat until it crackles.
Rest 25 minutes.
Carve so everyone gets skin and meat.

title: Gibanica
description: A layered cheese-and-egg filo pie, served as a Serbian festive side or vegetarian main.
notes: Sparkling water in the layers keeps the pie from going dense.
steps: Beat eggs with cottage cheese, crumbled feta and a little oil.
Layer crumpled filo with filling, splashing sparkling water as you go so the pie puffs.
Bake at 180°C until the top is dark gold and the centre set.
Rest 10 minutes.
Cut into squares.

title: Prebranac
description: Baked beans with a thick onion-paprika lid, a Serbian Lenten and Christmas Eve dish.
notes: The onion-to-bean ratio should look generous.
steps: Cook soaked beans with bay until tender; drain, keeping some liquor.
Cook onion in oil until brown, stir in paprika, and mix with the beans.
Bake in a dish at 180°C until the top darkens and the sauce is thick.
It should not be soupy.
Serve with bread and pickles.

title: Ajvar
description: Roasted pepper and aubergine relish, made ahead and opened for the Christmas table with bread and cheese.
notes: Low heat and stirring prevent catching.
steps: Roast peppers and aubergines until charred; peel and chop.
Cook in oil with garlic until thick and shiny, about an hour.
Season with salt and vinegar.
Cool the relish, then jar it for the Christmas table.
Serve at room temperature.

title: Serbian baklava with walnuts
description: Walnut baklava soaked in a lemon syrup, a Serbian slava and Christmas sweet.
notes: Lemon in the syrup is the Balkan habit versus rosewater-only versions.
steps: Layer filo brushed with butter, scattering ground walnuts every few sheets.
Cut into diamonds before baking at 170°C until gold.
Boil sugar, water and lemon into a syrup; cool slightly.
Pour cool syrup over hot baklava, or the other way around, so it soaks without sogging into mush.
Rest overnight before lifting pieces.

title: Čorba od pasulja
description: A Serbian bean soup with paprika and optional smoked meat, thicker than Bulgarian bob chorba and usually without mint.
notes: Distinct from Bulgarian bob chorba by smoked meat and no mint.
steps: Simmer soaked beans with onion, carrot and smoked pork until the beans cream.
Stir in paprika off the boil so it does not burn.
Taste for salt after the paprika goes in, because smoked meat varies.
Serve with bread and onion.
Skip pork for a Lenten pot.

title: Chocolate yule log with espresso cream
description: A cocoa sponge rolled around espresso cream and coated in ganache — a TDG yule log distinct from the French cacao bûche buttercream version.
notes: Do not duplicate the French bûche recipes; this filling is coffee, not buttercream.
steps: Bake a thin cocoa sponge from eggs, flour and cocoa; roll while warm and cool.
Whip cream with dissolved espresso and spread it inside the unrolled sponge; roll again.
Coat with ganache made from chocolate and a splash of cream.
Texture the surface with a fork and chill.
Slice with a hot knife to show the pale coffee spiral.

title: Rosemary roast chestnuts
description: Chestnuts roasted with rosemary and salt, an international winter nibble distinct from the French paper-cone method by the herb.
notes: The rosemary should perfume, not char to ash — tuck it under the nuts.
steps: Score each chestnut with an X.
Toss with oil, salt and rosemary.
Roast at 200°C until the shells peel back.
Steam in a towel five minutes, then peel.
Serve warm in a bowl.

title: Baked Camembert with garlic
description: A whole Camembert scored, studded with garlic, and baked until the middle runs — a party starter.
notes: A ripe cheese runs; a young one stays stubborn.
steps: Score the top rind in a cross-hatch and push in slivers of garlic and thyme.
Drizzle oil and bake at 180°C until the centre is liquid, about 15 minutes.
Serve in the box or dish with baguette.
Do not overbake or the cheese seizes.
Warn the table it is volcanic.

title: Garlic stuffed mushrooms
description: Mushroom caps filled with garlic crumbs and parsley, baked until the tops crisp.
notes: A vegetarian nibble that sits well beside smoked salmon.
steps: Pull the stems, chop them, and cook with garlic in butter.
Mix with breadcrumbs and parsley, then pack into the caps.
Bake at 190°C until the mushrooms are tender and the tops brown.
Serve the mushrooms hot from the oven while the crumbs still crunch.
Do not flood with butter or they stew.

title: Cinnamon hot chocolate
description: Real chocolate melted into milk with cinnamon, thicker than cocoa powder drinks.
notes: Use chocolate you like; powder cocoa is a different drink.
steps: Warm milk with cinnamon and salt; do not boil.
Whisk in chopped chocolate until smooth.
Sweeten to taste.
Froth with a whisk if you want a foam.
Serve immediately in warm mugs.

title: Vegan lentil and walnut loaf
description: A packed loaf of lentils, walnuts and oats that slices as a budget vegetarian Christmas main.
notes: Distinct from the UK cranberry nut roast by lentils and no eggs.
steps: Cook onion until sweet, then mix with lentils, chopped walnuts, oats, tomato paste and thyme.
Pack into a lined tin.
Bake at 180°C until the top is dry and browned.
Rest 15 minutes before slicing.
Serve with vegetarian gravy.

title: Mushroom stroganoff
description: A creamy paprika mushroom stew over noodles or rice, a vegetarian feast main that is not a loaf.
notes: Do not crowd the pan or the mushrooms steam.
steps: Brown mushrooms hard in butter so they colour; add onion.
Stir in paprika, then sour cream off the boil.
Cook noodles separately.
The sauce should be thick enough to cling.
Serve immediately.

title: Roasted squash soup
description: Butternut roasted until sweet, then blended with stock into a velvet starter for a vegetarian Christmas.
notes: Roasting beats boiling for flavour.
steps: Roast squash and onion with oil until the edges caramelise.
Simmer with stock, then blend until smooth.
Season with salt and nutmeg.
Loosen with water if it is too thick.
Serve in warm bowls.

title: Garlic hasselback potatoes
description: Potatoes sliced accordion-style, roasted with garlic butter until the edges frill — distinct from British goose-fat roasties.
notes: Waxy potatoes hold the slices; floury ones break.
steps: Slice potatoes thinly without cutting through, using chopsticks as a guard.
Brush with garlic butter, salt, and thyme.
Roast at 200°C, basting once, until the fans open and crisp.
They should be tender in the middle.
Serve as a side that is not a roast potato clone.

title: Overnight cinnamon rolls
description: Yeast rolls filled with cinnamon sugar, risen in the fridge overnight, baked Christmas morning.
notes: Overnight proof is the point; do not bake them the same evening.
steps: Make a yeast dough, roll it, spread with butter, brown sugar and cinnamon, and roll into a log.
Cut slices, arrange in a tin, and refrigerate overnight.
Bring to room temperature 30 minutes, then bake at 180°C until gold.
Ice with a little sugar glaze if you like.
Serve it warm, not piping, so the flavours stay clear.

title: Spiced fruit waffles
description: Waffles topped with warm cinnamon apples, a Christmas-morning plate that is not cinnamon rolls.
notes: Preheat the iron fully or the first waffle sticks.
steps: Whisk flour, eggs and milk into a waffle batter; rest 10 minutes.
Cook waffles until crisp.
Sauté apples in butter with cinnamon until they slump.
Spoon fruit over the waffles.
Serve at once so the waffle stays crisp.

title: Linzer cookies
description: Almond sandwich cookies with a jam window, an international cookie-tin classic distinct from Czech linecké by the almond meal.
notes: Almond meal is the Linzer tell versus plain Czech butter cookies.
steps: Make a dough with flour, almonds, butter and sugar; chill.
Cut pairs with windows in half of them.
Bake at 170°C until the edges colour.
Sandwich with jam and dust.
Fill the cookies only when they are completely cold so the jam stays put.

title: Jam thumbprint cookies
description: Butter cookies with a jam well pressed by a thumb, easy for children to help with.
notes: Apricot stays brighter than strawberry after baking.
steps: Beat butter and sugar, then flour and salt.
Roll balls, press a thumb well, and fill with jam.
Bake at 170°C until the edges just colour.
Cool on the tray so the jam sets.
Do not overfill or the jam floods.

title: Peppermint hot cocoa
description: Cocoa whisked with milk and crushed peppermint, a children's Christmas-eve mug.
notes: Distinct from the dark cinnamon chocolate drink.
steps: Whisk cocoa, sugar and salt with a splash of milk into a paste.
Add remaining milk and heat until steaming.
Crush peppermint and stir most of it in; save a little for the top.
Keep the cocoa below a boil so it stays smooth and not scorched.
Pour into warm mugs and add the last of the crushed peppermint on top.

title: Cocoa rum balls
description: An international no-bake rum ball using crushed biscuits and cocoa, distinct from Czech and German named versions by orange zest.
notes: Label them if children are grazing the cookie plate.
steps: Crush biscuits and mix with melted butter, cocoa, rum and orange zest.
Chill, roll, and coat in extra cocoa.
Chill the balls until they set firm enough to pile without smearing.
The orange zest is the TDG marker so they are not a clone of rumkugeln.
Keep the rum balls cool so the cocoa coating does not bloom.

title: Winter-fruit pavlova
description: A marshmallow-centred meringue piled with cream and winter citrus or pomegranate.
notes: Rainy kitchens hate meringue; pick a dry day.
steps: Whip whites to stiff peaks, then add sugar until glossy; fold in vinegar.
Bake a round at 120°C until the shell is dry and the inside is marshmallow, about 90 minutes; cool in the oven.
Whip cream and pile it on.
Top with orange segments and pomegranate.
Assemble just before serving.

title: Citrus bread pudding
description: Stale bread baked in custard with orange zest — a budget festive pudding that is not sticky toffee.
notes: Panettone leftovers can replace plain bread for a richer version.
steps: Cube bread into a buttered dish.
Whisk milk, eggs, sugar and orange zest; pour over and soak 15 minutes.
Bake at 170°C until the custard is set and the top is gold.
Rest 10 minutes.
Serve it warm, not piping, so the flavours stay clear.

title: Sparkling cranberry punch
description: A non-alcoholic punch of cranberry, orange and ginger ale for a family Christmas table.
notes: Use unsweetened cranberry if you can; otherwise skip extra sugar.
steps: Chill all the liquids.
Combine cranberry and orange juices in a bowl.
Add ginger ale just before serving so it stays lively.
Float orange slices and cranberries.
Do not mix hours ahead.

title: Warm cinnamon milk
description: Hot milk with cinnamon and a little honey, a bedtime Christmas-eve drink without cocoa.
notes: For a vegan cup, use oat milk and maple.
steps: Warm milk with cinnamon; do not boil.
Stir in honey and a pinch of nutmeg.
Strain if you used a stick and want a smooth cup.
Serve in small mugs.
Taste for sweetness; honey varies.

title: Roasted cauliflower steaks
description: Thick cauliflower slabs roasted until the edges char, a vegan main that is not a nut loaf.
notes: The trimmings roast alongside as florets so nothing is wasted.
steps: Cut cauliflower into 2 cm steaks, keeping the core so they hold.
Brush with oil, salt and paprika.
Roast at 220°C until the edges char and the stems are tender.
Finish with lemon juice.
Serve two steaks per person with a grain or lentils.

title: Chickpea and herb roast
description: A chickpea-bound roast with herbs, distinct from lentil-walnut and cranberry-nut versions.
notes: A third vegetarian main so households can pick textures.
steps: Mash chickpeas roughly with cooked onion, herbs, oil and breadcrumbs.
Pack into a tin.
Bake at 180°C until the outside is crisp.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
It should hold but still look rustic, not like pâté.

title: Spinach and ricotta cannelloni
description: Pasta tubes filled with spinach and ricotta, baked in tomato sauce — a make-ahead vegetarian feast dish.
notes: No-boil tubes need enough sauce; do not skimp.
steps: Wilt spinach, squeeze dry, and mix with ricotta, egg and half the parmesan.
Fill the tubes, lay in a dish, and cover with passata and remaining cheese.
Bake at 180°C until bubbling and the pasta is tender.
Rest 10 minutes.
Cover well so the pasta cooks in the sauce.

title: Oat apple crumble
description: Tart apples under an oat crumble, a budget winter pudding that is not pie.
notes: Bramley or other tart apples beat sweet eating apples here.
steps: Slice apples into a dish with cinnamon and a spoon of sugar.
Rub butter into flour, oats and remaining sugar to a clumpy crumb.
Scatter over the fruit and bake at 180°C until the fruit bubbles and the top is gold.
Rest 10 minutes.
Serve with cream or custard.

title: Cut-out sugar cookies
description: A straightforward butter-sugar dough for cutting trees and stars, made for icing with children.
notes: Overbaking turns them bitter; pull them when they look dry but not brown.
steps: Beat butter and sugar, add egg and vanilla, then flour and salt; chill 30 minutes.
Roll, cut shapes, and bake at 170°C until the edges barely colour.
Cool completely before icing.
They should stay pale.
Chill cut-outs on the tray if the kitchen is warm.

title: Florentines
description: Lacy nut-and-peel biscuits backed with chocolate, for a grown-up cookie tin.
notes: Line the tray well; they stick like caramel.
steps: Melt butter with sugar, stir in almonds, peel and flour.
Spoon small mounds with wide gaps; they spread.
Bake at 180°C until lacy and gold; reshape with a cutter while hot if needed.
Cool, then back with melted chocolate.
Set chocolate-side up to harden.

title: Meringue kisses
description: Small piped meringues dried in a low oven until they lift clean, for a gluten-free sweet plate.
notes: Humidity is the enemy; store with a silica pack if you have one.
steps: Whip whites with salt to stiff peaks, then add sugar until the meringue is glossy.
Fold in vanilla and pipe small kisses.
Dry at 110°C until they lift off the parchment, about an hour.
Cool in the oven.
They should be crisp throughout, unlike pavlova.

title: Christmas breakfast strata
description: A savoury bread-and-egg bake assembled the night before, with spinach and cheese.
notes: The overnight soak is what makes it custardy rather than eggy bread.
steps: Layer bread, wilted spinach and cheddar in a dish.
Whisk eggs, milk and salt, pour over, and refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 180°C until puffed and set.
Rest 10 minutes.
It should cut into squares like a savoury pudding.

title: Baked oats with pear
description: Oats baked with pear and cinnamon into a sliceable breakfast, quieter than cinnamon rolls.
notes: Use gluten-free oats if needed.
steps: Slice pears into a small baking dish.
Mix oats with eggs, milk, cinnamon and sugar; pour over.
Bake at 180°C until set and the pears are soft.
Rest five minutes.
Serve in bowls; it firms as it cools.

title: Orange-forward mulled wine
description: A party mulled wine with extra orange juice for body, distinct from UK, German, French and Nordic named pots by the juice ratio.
notes: This is the catch-all party jug when you are not making glühwein or glögg specifically.
steps: Warm wine with orange juice, orange slices, cinnamon, cloves and sugar.
Hold below a boil 15 minutes.
Strain into a thermos or jug.
Taste; the juice should make it rounder than wine-only pots.
Keep warm, not simmering.

title: Make-ahead onion gravy
description: A vegetarian onion gravy cooked the day before so the roast tray is less frantic.
notes: A vegetarian table can skip meat juices entirely.
steps: Cook onions in butter until they are deep brown, 20 minutes at least.
Stir in flour, then stock and soy.
Simmer until glossy.
Cool and refrigerate; reheat on the day, loosening with roasting juices if you have them.
Soy is for savouriness, not an Asian flavour — use a little.

title: Whole-berry cranberry sauce
description: Cranberries simmered with orange until they burst but stay saucy, distinct from the jellied New England mould.
notes: Do not confuse with the catalog's jellied cranberry sauce.
steps: Simmer cranberries with sugar, orange juice, zest and salt until most berries burst.
Stop while some remain whole.
Cool; it thickens as it sits.
Serve at room temperature.
This is a spooning sauce, not a sliceable jelly.

title: Rosemary focaccia for the table
description: A dimpled olive-oil bread with rosemary, for tearing beside soups and cheeses.
notes: A make-ahead dough can live in the fridge overnight.
steps: Mix flour, yeast, salt, water and most of the oil into a sticky dough; rise until doubled.
Stretch in an oiled tin, dimple, and stud with rosemary.
Drizzle remaining oil and bake at 220°C until gold.
Cool slightly, then tear.
The crumb should be open and oily in a good way.

title: Festive affogato
description: Vanilla ice cream drowned in hot espresso with a spoon of crushed amaretti — an instant Christmas dinner closer.
notes: The espresso must be hot or you get a sad puddle.
steps: Scoop ice cream into small glasses.
Crush amaretti over the top.
Pour hot espresso and a little amaretto over each scoop at the table.
Serve immediately so the contrast of hot and cold remains.
Skip amaretto for children and use extra espresso.

title: Rosemary spiced nuts
description: A tray of mixed nuts roasted with rosemary, chilli and a little sugar for the drinks table.
notes: Label clearly for nut-allergic guests — or skip this bowl entirely.
steps: Toss nuts with oil, sugar, salt, chilli and rosemary.
Roast at 170°C, stirring once, until they smell toasted.
Cool; they crisp as they sit.
Serve in a bowl.
Watch the sugar so it does not burn.

title: Orange olive-oil cake
description: A dairy-light orange cake that keeps well, useful when the oven is tired of logs and pies.
notes: Use a mild olive oil so the cake does not taste of pepper.
steps: Whisk eggs and sugar, then oil, orange zest and juice.
Fold in flour and baking powder.
Bake in a lined tin at 170°C until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool, then brush with a little extra juice if the top looks dry.
It keeps two days wrapped.

title: Quick pickled red onions
description: Red onions in a hot vinegar pickle, for brightening leftover plates and cheese boards.
notes: A make-ahead condiment, not a cooked vegetable side.
steps: Slice onions thinly and pack into a jar.
Heat vinegar, water, sugar and salt until dissolved, then pour over.
Cool, then refrigerate at least an hour.
They turn neon pink and stay crisp for a week.
Use on leftovers, gravlax plates, and cheese.

title: Cumin-glazed carrots
description: Carrots roasted with cumin and a little honey, a budget side distinct from the UK butter-sugar glaze.
notes: Different spice profile from the British Christmas glazed carrots.
steps: Toss carrots with oil, cumin and salt.
Roast at 200°C until they colour.
Drizzle honey and return for five minutes.
The cumin should be toasted, not raw.
Serve from the tin.

title: Celeriac rémoulade
description: Shredded celeriac in a mustard mayonnaise, a sharp make-ahead salad for rich meals.
notes: A French-leaning international salad; keep it in the general catalog for leftover platters.
steps: Peel and shred celeriac, then toss at once with lemon so it does not brown.
Fold in mayonnaise, mustard and salt.
Chill 30 minutes so the celeriac softens slightly.
It should taste punchy with mustard.
Serve cold beside ham or smoked fish.

title: Coffee old fashioned
description: A stirred whiskey drink with coffee liqueur and orange peel, for two after the dishes are done.
notes: Use a whiskey you like neat; the liqueur only whispers.
steps: Stir whiskey, coffee liqueur and water with ice until the glass frosts.
Strain into a small glass over fresh ice.
Twist orange peel over the drink and drop it in.
Serve immediately.
This is a nightcap, not a pitcher drink.
